stem: The long-term risk of stroke in valvular atrial fibrillation depends on clinical predictors, which are collectively assessed in the CHADS2 scoring scheme. Which of the following statement regarding CHADS2 score is correct?
options: CHADS is an acronym for Chronic renal failure, Hypertension, Age > 75 years, Diabetes mellitus, and prior Stroke.
The annual stroke risk with a CHADS2 score of 2 is 4%.
In the CHADS2 score age > 75 years has extra weight with 2 points.
In the CHADS2 score female gender is deemed high risk for stroke.
A 55-year-old male patient with new-onset atrial fibrillation and CHADS2 score of 0 is best managed with aspirin.

stem: The CHA2DS2-VASc score was developed to complement the CHADS2 score by the inclusion of additional ‘stroke risk modifier’ risk factors. Which of the following statements regarding CHA2DS2-VASc score is correct?
options: Male gender is an additional clinically relevant non-major stroke risk factor in CHA2DS2 score.
Presence of aortic plaque(s) carries more weight than peripheral vascular disease.
According to NICE guidelines stroke prevention therapy must be offered to any male aged < 65 years with atrial fibrillation and CHA2DS2-VASc score of 0.
A 57-year-old male with previous stroke and atrial fibrillation will have the same CHA2DS2-VASc score as an 80-year-old male with atrial fibrillation and no other risk factors.
A 49-year-old diabetic female with congestive heart failure and atrial fibrillation will have CHA2DS2-VASc score of 4.

stem: The REMATCH (Randomized Evaluation of Mechanical Assistance for the Treatment of Congestive Heart Failure) trial was conducted to determine the utility of the left ventricular assist device (LVAD) as a permanent form of circulatory support. Which of the following statements regarding the REMATCH trial is correct?
options: Patients were randomized to cardiac transplantation or HeartMate vented electric LVAD implantation.
The primary end point of the study was improvement in functional status at 1 month.
The survival of LVAD patients at 1 month was > 95%
The patients' New York Heart Association functional class remained the same at 1 month compared with base line.
99% of the LVAD patients had a serious event.

stem: Tricuspid valve surgery was first performed in 1963, and is currently performed in less than 5% of all cardiac surgical cases, in both the United Kingdom and North America. Redo tricuspid valve surgery is offered even less frequently due to association of high mortality and morbidity secondary to advanced heart failure symptoms with concomitant end-organ dysfunction. What is the in-hospital mortality for redo tricuspid valve surgery?

Tricuspid valve repair can be beneficial for patients with mild, moderate, or greater functional tricuspid regurgitation (TR) at the time of left-sided valve surgery with either tricuspid annular dilation or prior evidence of right heart failure. Which of the following statements regarding tricuspid valve repair for functional TR is correct?
options: Left uncorrected at the time of left-sided valve surgery, mild or moderate degrees of functional TR may progress over time in approximately 25% of patients and result in reduced long-term functional outcome and survival.
Tricuspid annulus dilation of 12 mm/m2 diameter indexed to body surface area on preoperative TTE is a risk factor for persistence and/or progression of TR.
A survival benefit with tricuspid repair in the setting of recent history of right heart failure has not been demonstrated.
Reoperation for severe, isolated TR after left-sided valve surgery is associated with a perioperative mortality rate of 30% to 50%.
Following repair with ring annuloplasty, residual TR is present in approximately 50% of patients at 5 years.

stem: The jugular venous pressure (JVP, sometimes referred to as jugular venous pulse) is the indirectly observed pressure over the venous system via visualization of the internal jugular vein. It can be useful in the differentiation of different forms of heart and lung disease. Which of the following statements regarding JVP is correct?
options: Classically JVP has two upward deflections and three downward deflections.
The ‘a wave’ corresponds to right ventricular contraction causing the tricuspid valve to bulge towards the right atrium. —
The ‘v wave’ corresponds to venous filling when the tricuspid valve is closed and venous pressure increases from venous return.
The ‘x’ descent follows the 'v' wave and occurs as a result of the right ventricle pulling the tricuspid valve downward during ventricular systole.
The ‘y’ descent corresponds to the rapid filling of the atrium following the closure of the tricuspid valve.

stem: A 63-year-old male patient after aortic valve replacement develops complete heart block and undergoes permanent pacemaker implantation. The procedure note shows the pacing mode as DDDR. What does R stand for in DDDR?
options: Rate-response pacing
Restore sinus rhythm
Repetitive pacing
Repetitive inhibition
Rebound rate trigger

stem: A 75-year-old female patient is diagnosed with sick sinus syndrome with intact atrioventricular conduction. She is offered a permanent pacemaker. What pacing mode will be best suited for this patient?
options: AAO
AAI
VVI
VDD
DDDR

stem: Protamine is used for neutralization of heparin during cardiac surgery. Which of the following statements regarding protamine is correct?
options: Protamine is a polycationic, acidic protein molecule, made up of two-thirds histidine residues and one-third other amino acids.
A fixed dose of 2.0 mg of protamine for 1 mg or 100 units of heparin is used to neutralize heparin.
An overdose of protamine causes platelet dysfunction.
Free protamine increases fibrinogen levels.
Free protamine enhances the procoagulant effect of thrombin.

stem: The Endobronchial Valve for Emphysema Palliation (VENT) trial was conducted to assess the safety and efficacy of endobronchial valves in advanced emphysema. Which of the following statements regarding the VENT trial is correct?
options: The trial compared unilateral treatment with endobronchial valves with lung volume reduction surgery.
Efficacy end points were percent changes in the forced vital capacity and reduction in lung volume.
At 6 months there was no difference in forced expiratory volume in 1 second between the two groups.
At 12 months, the rate of the complications composite was more in the endobronchial valve group compared with the control group.
At 90 days, in the endobronchial valve group there were decreased rates of exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring hospitalization versus in the control group.

stem: Antithrombin III is a small protein molecule that inactivates several enzymes of the coagulation system and plays an important role in regulating normal blood coagulation. Which of the following statements regarding antithrombin III is correct?
options: It is a glycoprotein produced by the bone marrow and consists of 432 amino acids.
Its activity is decreased by heparin.
The physiological target proteases of antithrombin are those of the extrinsic (tissue factor) pathway.
It has a half-life in blood of around 3 days.
Its deficiency generally comes to light when a patient suffers recurrent haemorrhage.

stem: A 46-year-old patient with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) underwent rigid bronchoscopy. Which of the following sterilization techniques will inactivate the CJD prion?
options: Autoclave at 134C for 18 minutes in a prevacuum sterilizer.
Boiling
Dry heat
Ethylene oxide
Hydrogen peroxide gas plasma

stem: A 45-year-old male patient with chest pain, cough and fever for more than 4 weeks had a contrast-enhanced CT scan after an abnormality was identified on plain chest radiograph. What pathology is most likely demonstrated by the contrast-enhanced CT scan shown below?
options: Pericardial lipoma
Pericardial cyst
Pericardial lipoblastoma
Pericardial paraganglioma
Germ cell tumour

stem: The long axis transoesophageal echocardiogram image (Figure A) was obtained from a 48-year-old man with a 2-year history of intermittent fever. Photograph (Figure B) shows the variegated gelatinous mass with multiple excrescences that was excised at surgery. Which of the following statements regarding this pathology is true?
options: Approximately 50% of these masses are found in the left atrium.
A female predominance has been reported for this pathology.
Approximately 80% of patients with this pathology are asymptomatic.
This pathology is an endocardial-based mass that infiltrates the underlying tissues.
This pathology mainly affects patients in the sixth and seventh decades of life.

stem: The transthoracic four-chamber echocardiogram (Figure A) shows a rounded echogenic mass (arrow) attached to the apex of the left ventricle in a 69-year-old man with chronic atrial fibrillation. Photograph (Figure B) of the excised specimen shows a gelatinous, multilobular, papillary mass. Which of the following statements regarding this pathology is true?
options: This pathology accounts for three-fourths of all cardiac valvular tumours.
A male predominance has been reported for this pathology.
Patients have a mean age of 30 years.
Recurrence after surgical resection occurs in more than 50% cases.
This is usually a highly vascular pathology.

stem: The chest radiograph and CT scan shown below were obtained in a 25-year-old man with a typical carcinoid tumour. Which of the following statements regarding carcinoid tumours is correct?
options: Pulmonary or bronchial carcinoid tumours account for over 25% of all pulmonary neoplasms.
About 10%-20% of pulmonary carcinoids are typical carcinoids.
Patients with atypical carcinoids are more frequently men.
Patients with atypical carcinoids are about 10 years younger than those with typical carcinoids.
The overall 5-year survival rate for typical carcinoids is 56%.

stem: Digoxin is the oldest cardiac medication used in contemporary medicine. It has a complex pharmacokinetic profile and narrow therapeutic index. Which of the following statements regarding digoxin is correct?
options: Its primary mechanism action is inhibition of the H+-K+ ATPase pump.
It has parasympatholytic actions.
Biliary excretion is responsible for 50% to 70% of digoxin clearance.
Serum digoxin concentration is elevated in patients with higher lean body weight compared with their low lean body weight counterparts.
Compared with subjects not receiving glycosides, it increases mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation and heart failure.

stem: The imaging investigations below show a mediastinal mass in a 35-year old woman who complains of dysphagia. The most likely diagnosis is
options: Duplication cyst
Oesophageal fibrovascular polyp
Oesophageal leiomyoma
Schwannoma
Tuberculous mediastinal lymphadenitis

stem: The CT scan shown below is from a 50-year-old woman with cystic oesophageal duplication. Which of the following statements regarding oesophageal duplication cysts is correct?
options: Oesophageal duplication cysts account for 25% of all tumours or tumour-like lesions of the oesophagus.
Most oesophageal duplication cysts communicate directly with the oesophageal lumen.
Most adults with oesophageal duplication cysts are asymptomatic.
CT scans of cystic oesophageal duplication depict a heterogeneous mass with low attenuation and a rough border.
At T2-weighted MR imaging, duplication cysts may show low signal intensity and a poorly defined margin.

stem: The double contrast oesophagogram in a 76-year-old diabetic man has a cobblestone appearance in the proximal oesophagus while the mid and distal oesophagus has a shaggy appearance, and grossly irregular contour, due to the presence of multiple plaques and ulcers. Pseudomembrane is also seen as double tracts which parallel the oesophagus. Which of the following conditions is most likely to give rise to this appearance?
options: Barrett’s oesophagus
Behcet’s disease
Candida oesophagitis
Scleroderma
Tuberculosis

stem: Lung window of thin-section (1-mm collimation) CT scan obtained at the level of the liver dome in a 59-year-old male shows a dilated oesophagus (arrows), a moderate amount of pericardial effusion (open arrows), and left pleural effusion (curved arrows). Also note the occurrence of pulmonary change consisting of irregular linear opacities, ground-glass opacities, and honeycombing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Achalasia
Candida oesophagitis
Reflux oesophagitis
Scleroderma
Tuberculosis

stem: A 50-year-old woman had complete resection of a stage 3 thymoma. What 5-year survival rate will be quoted to this patient?
A 23-year-old man is diagnosed with primary mediastinal seminoma. Which of the following statements regarding primary mediastinal seminoma is correct?
options: Primary mediastinal seminomas comprise 75 to 80% of malignant mediastinal germ cell tumours.
Radiographically, seminomas are bulky, lobulated, homogenous masses.
Local invasion is a common feature of mediastinal seminoma.
Seminomas are uniquely resistant to radiation therapy.
Chemotherapy alone gives a 20% 5-year disease-free survival rate.

stem: The CT image shown below was obtained in a 55-year-old patient with sarcoidosis and recurrent haemoptysis. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is true?
options: It usually invades the surrounding lung parenchyma or blood vessels.
The lesion shown may decrease in size or resolve spontaneously without treatment in 50% of cases.
Sputum cultures for causative organisms are positive only in 50% of cases.
Bronchial artery embolization is the treatment of choice in cases of recurrent haemoptysis.
Surgical resection is indicated in patient with life-threatening haemoptysis and poor functional reserve.

stem: The radial artery (RA) was reintroduced in coronary surgery in the early 1990s and currently represents an alternative to the right internal thoracic artery (ITA) as a second arterial conduit. The RA has peculiar morphologic and functional features that distinguish it from the other arterial grafts, with major surgical implications. Which of the following statements regarding the morpho-functional features of the RA is true?
options: The RA is an elastic conductance artery.
In humans the mean length of the RA is 12.5 cm.
The main feature of the RA is the thick adventitia.
Compared with the ITA the RA has a significantly greater intima to media ratio.
The prevalence of intimal hyperplasia is known to be higher in the ITA than in the RA.

stem: The Saphenous Vein Versus Right Internal Thoracic Artery as a Y-Composite Graft (SAVE RITA) trial was designed to evaluate the noninferiority of the saphenous vein (SV) compared with the right internal thoracic artery (RITA) used as a Y-composite graft. Which of the following statements regarding this trial is correct?
options: The primary endpoint was 1-year freedom from repeat revascularisation.
The 1-year patency rate of the SV composite grafts was inferior to that of the RITA composite grafts.
The overall survival rates were significantly superior for the RITA group at 1 and 4 years.
The overall graft patency rate was 85% at 1 year.
No statistically significant differences were found between the 2 groups in the freedom from major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular event rates at 1 and 4 years.

stem: Adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) now plays a significant role in the treatment of resected non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients and has become standard in clinical practice. It took more than two decades of clinical research to show its value. The Lung Adjuvant Cisplatin Evaluation (LACE) meta-analysis is the most important piece of evidence in this regard. Which of the following statements regarding LACE meta-analysis is correct?
options: The benefit of cisplatin adjuvant chemotherapy varied with cancer stage.
The drug given with cisplatin modified the effect of chemotherapy.
The effect of chemotherapy was not influenced by the performance status of the patients.
The effect of chemotherapy was greater in female patients.
The effect of chemotherapy was greater in patient with adenocarcinoma.

stem: A 65-year-old man experienced an inferior wall myocardial infarction. On the third post-infarction day, a new systolic murmur was heard. The patient remained asymptomatic. Coronary angiography revealed an occluded right coronary artery with no important disease in the left system. The left ventriculogram is shown below. The best treatment is
options: continued medical management for four to six weeks followed by surgical repair.
coronary bypass of the right coronary artery and mitral valve repair.
medical management alone for 4 to 6 weeks to allow recovery from acute infarct.
percutaneous angioplasty of the right coronary artery.
urgent surgical repair.

stem: A 55-year-old patient could not be weaned from bypass following porcine mitral and aortic valve replacements coupled with coronary artery bypass grafting. Suitable haemodynamics were obtained with a left ventricular assist device. The patient has no native ventricular ejection after seven days. The most appropriate next step is to
options: continue assist pumping for two to three weeks to allow for recovery.
perform a cardiac catheterisation and ventriculogram.
perform a myocardial viability study.
perform transoesophageal echocardiography.
perform cardiac transplantation.

stem: A 50-year-old man could not be weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass following coronary artery bypass grafting despite inotropic and intra-aortic balloon support. Satisfactory haemodynamics are achieved after insertion of a left ventricular assist device. However, profound cyanosis is noted by the anesthetist. The next appropriate step in management is
options: aggressive medical management of right ventricular failure.
insertion of a right ventricular assist device.
pulmonary embolectomy.
repositioning of the inlet cannula.
transoesophageal or epicardial echocardiography.

stem: Myocyte contraction is the primary factor determining myocardial oxygen consumption above basal levels. The clinical technique used for assist pumping in postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock which most effectively decreases left ventricular myocardial oxygen consumption is
options: intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation.
left atrial-to-aortic pulsatile asynchronous assist pumping.
left ventricular-to-aortic pulsatile synchronous assist pumping.
nonpulsatile left atrial-to-aortic assist pumping.
veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

stem: A 53-year-old man with tuberculosis was admitted with massive haemoptysis. A current chest radiograph is shown below. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step to control this patient’s bleeding?
options: bronchial artery embolization
bronchoscopy with bronchial occlusion
immediate right upper lobectomy
position the patient left side down
sedation and assisted mechanical ventilation

stem: A 38-year-old man involved in a high-speed head-on collision required prolonged ventilation and tracheostomy because of pulmonary contusion with concomitant adult respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) but eventually recovered. Shortly after discharge, he returned to the clinic complaining of shortness of breath and limited exercise capacity. A chest computed tomographic scan was obtained and a representative cut from this scan is shown. The most likely cause of the tomographic finding is
options: barotrauma.
chylothorax.
empyema.
pre-existing lung abnormality.
pulmonary abscess.

stem: A 66-year-old man is to undergo elective mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve repair. Shortly after placing and inflating a balloon-tipped pulmonary artery catheter, the anesthetist notes blood in the endotracheal tube. The blood is suctioned and there does not appear to be ongoing bleeding. Recommended management is to
options: localize the site of bleeding by bronchoscopy and place an endobronchial blocker until heparin is reversed.
open the pleural space. If there is visible parenchymal haemorrhage, perform a lobectomy.
perform flexible bronchoscopy. If there is no active bleeding, proceed with planned operation.
postpone the operation.
reposition the catheter and avoid further balloon inflation.

stem: A 58-year-old man with good preoperative pulmonary function underwent a right pneumonectomy for lung cancer. His first 24 hours after operation were uneventful. Shortly thereafter he is noted to become apprehensive, and progressive dyspnea and hypoxia ensue. During his evaluation a chest x-ray is obtained. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: bronchopleural fistula
pneumonia
pneumothorax
pulmonary oedema
pulmonary embolus

stem: An 80-year-old man developed a haemothorax after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation. A left chest tube was placed, and after 48 hours a chest x-ray was taken which shows a large residual haemothorax. A second more dependent chest tube was placed under ultrasound guidance. Drainage is minimal and the chest x-ray remains unchanged. Appropriate management at this point is
options: addition of a third chest tube to improve drainage.
instillation of streptokinase into the chest tube.
observation to allow time for hemolysis and drainage.
thoracoscopy and evacuation of the haemothorax.
thoracotomy, decortication and drainage.

stem: Lung transplantation has been the last of the solid organs to gain attraction as a viable therapeutic option. Nonetheless, there have been incremental advances in lung transplantation, including liberalization of criteria for both suitable donor organs as well as acceptable recipients. Which of the following statements regarding disease considerations for lung transplantation is correct?
options: Infection with pan-resistant Burkholderia cepacia does not affect early mortality.
Lung transplant should be delayed as long as possible in young women with cystic fibrosis.
Medical treatment of primary S pulmonary hypertension relieves symptoms in the minority of patients
Lung transplantation is particularly effective in patients with Eisenmenger syndrome
Patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis have the highest mortality on the waiting list.

stem: Radiologic imaging is an essential component of clinical staging of lung cancer. Which of the following statements regarding radiologic imaging for clinical staging of lung cancer is correct?
options: A node is considered positive on CT scan if the size exceeds 1.5 cm
CT predicts nodal metastasis with 85% sensitivity
Standardized uptake value > 2.0 is an abnormal PET scan.
PET has sensitivity and specificity exceeding 80%.
Combining PET and CT does not appreciably improve diagnostic accuracy.

stem: Accurate staging and restaging of primary tumour and mediastinal nodes in patients with lung cancer is of significant importance. Which of the following statements regarding lung cancer staging is correct?
options: MRI has no advantage over CT scan
Less than 20% of patients with a new diagnosis of lung cancer will have metastatic disease
Percutaneous transthoracic needle biopsy has a high false positive rate
Transbronchial needle aspiration is particularly effective for paraoesophageal node biopsy
VATS sensitivity and specificity approaches 100%

stem: Malignant pleural effusions are the second leading cause of exudative pleural effusions after parapneumonic effusions. In the vast majority of cases, a malignant pleural effusion signifies incurable disease associated with high morbidity and mortality. Which of the following statements regarding malignant pleural effusion is correct?
options: About 50% of patients with lung cancer will develop a malignant effusion.
High glucose and high pH levels are common.
Nodular pleural thickening is suggestive of malignant effusion on CT scan.
The most common cause of elevated pleural amylase is pancreatic pseudocyst.
Undirected pleural needle biopsy is superior to VATS for cytology.

stem: Advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is a significant cause of morbidity. Treatment options beyond conventional medical therapies are limited to a minority of patients. Lung volume reduction surgery (LVRS) although effective in selected subgroups of patients is not commonly undertaken. Which of the following statements regarding lung volume reduction surgery is correct?
options: FEV1 gains are modest at best, with only 20% improvement in bilateral operations
Homogeneously distributed emphysema is an indication for LVRS
Marked hyperinflation excludes patients from LVRS
Patients with predominant upper lobe disease and low exercise capacity fare best with surgery compared to medical treatment
VATS LVRS had a lower surgical mortality than sternotomy in the NET trial

stem: Oesophageal ultrasound can define both T and N staging of oesophageal carcinoma. Which of the following correlations regarding oesophageal ultrasound is correct?
options: CT scanning is more accurate for staging oesophageal cancer.
The fourth layer is the paraoesophageal tissue.
The most hyperechoic layer is the epithelium and lamina propria.
The muscularis mucosa is white.
The submucosa is hypoechoic.

stem: Due to close anatomical relationship between the upper oesophagus and the tracheobronchial tree, many patients with advanced oesophageal cancer will suffer from airway complications. These include airway stenosis or esophago-respiratory fistulation. Airway stenting is proven to offer effective palliation for patients with both these complications. Which of the following statements regarding stenting of the airway and oesophagus is correct?
options: Airway stenting is contraindicated in lung transplant patients due to high rates of restenosis.
Covered stents reduce the risk of migration.
Oesophageal stenting for palliation reduces complications of adjuvant therapy for oesophageal cancer.
Silicone stents are effective at preventing recurrent dysphagia.
Silicone stents are preferred for benign airway strictures.

stem: Oesophageal manometry is a specialized procedure used to evaluate lower and upper oesophageal sphincter pressure, oesophageal body contraction amplitude, and peristaltic sequence. The procedure is clinically useful in evaluation of a patient with nonstructural dysphagia, unexplained or noncardiac chest pain, a compendium of symptoms suggested because of gastrooesophageal reflux disease, and in the preoperative evaluation for antireflux surgery. Which of the following statements regarding oesophageal manometry is correct?
options: The lower border of the lower oesophageal sphincter (LOS) is identified as the point where sphincter pressure equals the oesophageal baseline.
The respiratory inversion point is the functional division between the chest and the abdomen.
An average abdominal length of the LOS less than 2 cm is abnormal.
An average LOS pressure less than 10 mm Hg is abnormal.
The LOS pressure normally does not drop to gastric baseline until the peristaltic wave meets the LOS.

stem: Solitary fibrous tumours of the pleura are rare and slow-growing neoplasms originating from the mesenchymal tissue underlying the mesothelial layer of the pleura. These tumours may have an unpredictable clinical course. Which of the following statements regarding systemic effects of solitary fibrous tumours of the pleura is correct?
options: Patients may present with seizure or coma.
Smaller tumours are more likely to produce hypoglycemia.
The production of ADH-like substances is thought to be the underlying cause.
Hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy does not resolve after tumour resection.
Up to 25% of tumours will present with hypoglycemia.

stem: Malignant pleural mesothelioma is an uncommon neoplasm, and the prognosis for this disease is poor. Which of the following statements regarding staging of malignant pleural mesothelioma according to the IMIG staging system is correct?
options: T1a = nontransmural involvement of pericardium
T1b = tumour limited to parietal pleura
T2 = involvement of diaphragmatic muscle
T3 = extension of tumour into pulmonary parenchyma
T4 = involvement of endothoracic fascia

stem: Resection of lung metastases from colorectal cancer is increasingly performed with a curative intent. Which of the following statements regarding pulmonary metastasis from colorectal carcinoma is correct?
options: A normal CEA level prior to thoracotomy is a positive prognostic factor.
Dual metastatectomy is associated with poor survival.
Five-year survival is less than 20%.
Patients with a pulmonary metastasis after a hepatic resection do not benefit from pulmonary resection.
A solitary pulmonary nodule in a colorectal cancer patient most likely represents a metastatic lesion

stem: The five-year survival rate is a type of survival rate for estimating the prognosis of a particular disease, normally calculated from the point of diagnosis. Which of the following is correct concerning 5-year survival rates after pulmonary metastasectomy?
options: Breast cancer: 10-20%
Germ cell tumours: 20%
Head and neck cancer: 10-15%
Melanoma: 20-35%
Renal cell cancer: 60-70%

stem: Thoracic outlet syndrome is a well-described disorder caused by thoracic outlet compression of the brachial plexus and/or the subclavian vessels. Which of the following statements regarding anatomy of the thoracic outlet is correct?
options: The distal division of the cervicoaxillary canal is most important for neurovascular compression.
The anteromedial costoclavicular space contains the subclavian vessels.
The scalene triangle contains the brachial plexus.
The scalenus anticus depresses the first rib, narrowing the costoclavicular space.
The upper type of scalenus anticus syndrome involves compression of C7 and C8 nerve roots

stem: Palmoplantar hyperhidrosis can be an incapacitating medical condition because it not only hinders patient quality of life but also causes the secondary effect of excess cutaneous sweat. Which of the following statements regarding the presentation of hyperhidrosis is correct?
options: Symptoms are typically worse during the winter months.
Almost all patients with palmar hyperhidrosis also have plantar hyperhidrosis.
Less than 10% will have concomitant bromhidrosis.
Fungal infections are common.
The sporadic form is much more common than familial forms.

stem: Blunt thoracic trauma can result in significant morbidity in injured patients. Both chest wall and the intrathoracic visceral injuries can lead to life-threatening complications if not anticipated and treated. Which of the following statements regarding blunt trauma to the chest wall is correct?
options: Clavicular fracture is the most common blunt thoracic injury.
Acute respiratory distress syndrome is less common than pulmonary contusion in the setting of flail chest.
Scapular fractures are most common at the coracoid process.
The number of rib fractures is not associated with the presence of pneumothorax.
Chest CT is recommended for full evaluation of clavicular and scapular fractures.

stem: Laryngotracheal resection and reconstruction is a recognized treatment option for postintubation subglottic stenosis. Which of the following is true regarding laryngotracheal resection?
options: The recurrent laryngeal nerves are protected by incorporating a beveled resection.
Cricoid reconstruction is best performed with a continuous nonabsorbable suture.
Posterior resection of the cricoid should be full thickness with a generous posterior tracheal bevel.
Incision through the cricoid membrane should be avoided in order to prevent injury to the true vocal cords.
Sutures through the membranous wall of the trachea are secured to the membranous portion of the cricoid plate.

stem: The most important reason for cardiac catheterisation in the preoperative evaluation of a two year old child with a ventricular septal defect (VSD) is to determine
options: coronary artery anatomy.
if additional VSDs exist.
location of the VSD.
pulmonary vascular resistance.
relationship of the VSD to the tricuspid valve.

stem: A 53-year-old woman with terminal ileitis underwent aortic valve replacement for bacterial endocarditis. At operation, she was found to have infection of the non-coronary leaflet that extended to the annulus. Reconstruction of the annulus and aortic valve replacement was performed. The patient was haemodynamically stable. A rhythm strip from her early postoperative course shows junctional tachycardia without evidence of sinus node function. The best course of management of this rhythm disturbance is
options: digoxin therapy to slow the ventricular response.
electrophysiologic study to determine conduction characteristics of the atrioventricular node.
insertion of permanent pacemaker.
observation.
temporary pacing using pacing wires placed at operation.

stem: A 65-year-old man presented to the emergency department after a syncopal episode. During initial evaluation, he experienced ventricular tachycardia which progressed to ventricular fibrillation. After defibrillation he was admitted to the Coronary Care Unit. Over the next 48 hours, he had four episodes of haemodynamically compromising ventricular tachycardia unresponsive to lidocaine and procainamide. Cardiac catheterisation and coronary angiography subsequently demonstrated occlusion of a dominant right coronary artery, 60% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD), and a normal circumflex coronary artery. Ventriculography shows inferior aneurysm. Which of the following is the best approach to the patient problem?
options: angioplasty of the LAD coronary artery
angioplasty of the LAD coronary artery and defibrillator insertion
coronary artery bypass grafting and defibrillator insertion
coronary artery bypass grafting and left ventricular aneurysmectomy
left ventricular aneurysmectomy alone

stem: A 78-year-old obese female with insulin-dependent diabetes has a patent left internal mammary artery (LIMA) to a large circumflex artery. The inferior wall is akinetic from an old infarction. She is undergoing bypass grafting to the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery because of a symptomatic 2 cm long 60% proximal LAD stenosis. Intraoperative transoesophageal echocardiography reveals minimal disease of the ascending aorta and severe intramural atherosclerotic disease of the arch. The best operative strategy is to
options: close the chest, wait two days and place an intraluminal stent in the LAD coronary artery followed by six weeks of dual antiplatelet therapy.

proceed with cardiopulmonary bypass using the femoral artery for arterial cannulation. Cool the patient to 18°C and replace the arch under total circulatory arrest. Use cardioplegic arrest for the heart and perform a vein graft to the LAD.

proceed with cardiopulmonary bypass using the femoral artery for arterial cannulation. Cool the patient to 25°C, maintaining mean blood pressure above 70 mmHg. Use the right internal mammary artery to bypass the LAD while the heart is vented and fibrillating. Place no clamps on or cannulae in the aorta.

use the echocardiographic image to choose a cannulation site on the ascending aorta. Cool the patient to 25°C, maintaining mean blood pressure above 70 mmHg. Use the right internal mammary artery to bypass the LAD while the heart is vented and fibrillating. Place no clamps on the aorta.

use the echocardiographic image to choose cannulation and clamp sites on the ascending aorta. Using cardioplegic arrest, perform a saphenous vein graft to the LAD with a single clamp technique (perform the proximal anastomosis during the cross-clamp interval).

stem: A 66-year-old male patient with previous stented bioprosthetic valve is to undergo a second (repeat) aortic valve replacement due to prosthetic valve endocarditis. It is suggested to utilize aprotinin infusion to minimize blood usage. The perfusionist must modify the standard techniques during bypass by
options: avoiding use of ultrafiltration.
inducing urine output of >3 ml/minute.
keeping perfusion pressure >80 mmHg.
monitoring anticoagulation by heparin titration.
not using cell saver salvaged blood.

stem: A 45-year-old underwent uneventful mitral valve replacement for rheumatic mixed mitral valve disease. Ten minutes after rewarming has begun, the perfusionist reports that the mixed venous oxygen saturation is 47%. Bypass flow is 2.4 l/min/m2, mean systemic blood pressure is 80 mmHg, arterial oxygen saturation is 100%, hematocrit is 23%, bladder temperature is 36°C and the patient’s hands and feet are cold. The most appropriate action is to
options: add packed cells to the bypass circuit.
allow the patient to eject to provide pulsatile flow and improve peripheral warming.
check the ionized calcium level.
deepen the level of anaesthesia.
increase the flow rate to 3.3 l/[min*m2].

stem: A 55-year-old man has undergone aortic arch replacement with 45 minutes of total circulatory arrest at 18°C. The patient’s temperature is 34°C. Rewarming preliminary to the termination of cardiopulmonary bypass may best be facilitated by
options: transfer of volume from the bypass circuit to the heart to allow cardiac ejection.
use of small doses of phenylephrine to increase perfusion pressure to 80 mmHg to improve peripheral perfusion.
ventilation with humidified oxygen heated to 40°C.
warming of the blood in the bypass circuit to 37°C during the period of circulatory arrest.
use aprotinin.

stem: Off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and on-pump CABG are two well-established therapeutic strategies for patients with coronary artery disease. However, there is an ongoing debate regarding which strategy provides superior graft patency. Which of the following statements regarding the current best available evidence assessing the impact of off-pump CABG compared to on-pump CABG on graft patency is correct?
options: Similar risk of occlusion of all grafts after off-pump and on-pump CABG.
Significant difference in occlusion of left internal mammary artery grafts between off-pump and on-pump CABG.
Increased risk of occlusion of radial artery grafts after off-pump CABG.
Increased risk of occlusion of saphenous vein grafts after off-pump CABG.
Increased risk of occlusion of all grafts after on-pump CABG.

stem: The German Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Elderly Patients (GOPCABE) study focused exclusively on patients 75 years of age or older to clarify the potential benefit of off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in high-risk patients. Which of the following statements regarding the GOPCABE trial is correct?
options: The primary end point was death at 30 days and 12 months after surgery.
Stroke occurred more frequently in the on-pump CABG group.
At 12 months, there was no significant between-group difference in the composite end point.
At 30 days, repeat revascularisation occurred more frequently after on-pump CABG than after off-pump CABG.
In patients 75 years of age or older, off-pump CABG is a superior strategy compared to on-pump CABG.

stem: The cardiac action potential differs significantly in different portions of the heart. The heart is provided with a special excitatory system and a contractile system necessary to differentiate action potentials in the heart, which allow this organ to function at a constant rate. The following data were obtained from intracellular recordings of cardiac cells. Cell A Cell B Cell C Resting membrane potential (mV) − 50 − 60 − 80 Capacity for diastolic depolarization Yes Yes No Intrinsic rate of depolarization (beats/min) 90 45 None Cell A would most likely be found in the
options: sinoatrial (SA) node
atrial muscle -
atrioventricular (AV) node
Purkinje fibers
ventricular muscle

stem: A 55-year-old man who has smoked two packs of cigarettes a day for 35 years complains of shortness of breath, chronic cough, and production of yellowish, foul-smelling sputum. He has clubbing of his finger nails and the nail beds and lips are noted to be cyanotic. Arterial blood gas analysis of this patient reveals the following: Po2 = 55 mm Hg, Pco2 = 56 mm Hg, HCO3− = 35 mEq/L, and pH = 7.4. These blood gas data are most consistent with
options: acute respiratory failure
inadequate alveolar ventilation
anatomic shunt
anemia
carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning

stem: The partial pressure of gas in blood is significant because it is directly related to ventilation and oxygenation. When the arterial O2 tension drops from 100 mm Hg to 27 mm Hg with an arterial pH of 7.4 and a CO2 tension of 40 mm Hg, O2 content in the blood decreases by about
A 38-year-old man is admitted to the hospital with suspected partially compensated respiratory acidosis. Which of the following sets of laboratory data would confirm this suspicion?
options: [HCO3−] 17 mEq/L; Pco2 19 mm Hg; pH 7.9
[HCO3−] 31 mEq/L; Pco2 80 mm Hg; pH 7.22
[HCO3−] 9.8 mEq/L; Pco2 30 mm Hg; pH 7.14
[HCO3−] 24 mEq/L; Pco2 45 mm Hg; pH 7.5
[HCO3−] 20 mEq/L; Pco2 25 mm Hg; pH 7.5

stem: A 46-year-old lightly anesthetized man, who underwent right upper lobectomy, is breathing spontaneously with a cardiac output of 6 L/min, a heart rate of 75 beats/min, an O2 consumption of 240 ml/min, and a mixed venous O2 tension of 40 mm Hg. He is ventilated for 10 minutes at his normal tidal volume but at twice the normal frequency with a gas mixture that is 20% O2 and 80% N2. The airway pressure at the end of inspiration is 5 cm H2O. On cessation of artificial ventilation, the patient does not breathe for 1 minute. The most important factor responsible for the temporary apnea in this patient is reduced activity of the
options: peripheral chemoreceptors, because of the high O2 tension
peripheral chemoreceptors, because of the low CO2 tension
pulmonary stretch receptors that inhibit inspiration
medullary chemoreceptors, because of the low CO2 tension
medullary chemoreceptors, because of the high O2 tension

stem: A man undergoes lung volume studies using the helium dilution method. The test begins at the end of a normal expiration. The initial fraction of helium in the spirometer is 0.05, and the helium fraction after equilibration with the lungs is 0.03. The volume of gas in the spirometer is kept constant at 4 L during the procedure by the addition of O2. According to a spirogram, this patient’s vital capacity (VC) is 5 L and his expiratory reserve volume (ERV) is 2 L. What is this patient’s functional residual capacity (FRC)?

The following arterial blood data are obtained from a patient who is cyanotic at rest: Po2 = 60 mm Hg, haemoglobin saturation = 85%, Pco2 = 40 mm Hg, pH = 7.39, and haemoglobin concentration = 18 g/dl. The arterial O2 tension rises to 295 mm Hg after the patient breathes 100% O2 at sea level for 20 minutes. Cardiac catheterisation reveals normal pressures and an O2 tension of 40 mm Hg in the right atrium, right ventricle, and pulmonary artery while the patient breathes 100% O2. What fraction of the cardiac output is represented by shunted blood?

An elderly woman visits the hospital in emergency department with the recent onset of grotesque swelling of the right arm, neck and face. Her right jugular vein is visibly engorged and her right brachial pulse is diminished. On the basis of these signs her chest X-ray might show:
options: A left cervical rib
A mass in the upper lobe of the right lung
Aneurysm of the aortic arch
Right pneumothorax
Thoracic duct blockage in the posterior mediastinum

stem: While carbon dioxide is a metabolic waste product, it plays some important physiological roles as well. Carbon dioxide is carried in the blood principally in the form of:
options: Free carbon dioxide
Carbonic acid
Bicarbonate
Carbaminohaemoglobin
Carbon monoxide -

stem: Cystic fibrosis is a serious inherited disease which mainly affects the lungs and pancreas but can involve other organs. Symptoms usually begin in early childhood and include persistent cough, wheeze, repeated chest infections, difficulty absorbing food and general ill health. Which of the following statements about cystic fibrosis is correct?
options: Sweat of cystic fibrosis patients has elevated Na+ and low Cl− content.
The gene that is abnormal in cystic fibrosis encodes a cAMP regulated Cl− channel.
Cystic fibrosis is more common in African-Americans than in Caucasians.
The gene that is abnormal in cystic fibrosis is located on the X chromosome.
Cystic fibrosis is caused by a defective Na+ transporter across airway epithelial cells, resulting in thick airway mucus.

stem: Complications in tracheal surgery are not uncommon but generally do not influence the final result. Precise information about the extent of the diseased tracheal part as well as thorough planning of the operative procedure, meticulous dissection, and knowledge of release maneuvers by an experienced thoracic surgeon will diminish the risk of adverse effects. Which of the following statements regarding results of tracheal resections is correct?
options: The principal morbidity from tracheal resection for idiopathic laryngotracheal stenosis is dysphagia.
Operative mortality for tracheooesophageal fistula is lower than for primary tumours.
Long-term survival after resection for squamous cell carcinoma is better than for adenoid cystic carcinoma.
Resection for invasive thyroid cancer is not indicated.
Lymph node status does not affect long-term survival after tracheal resection.

stem: Penetrating injuries to the chest encompass ballistic and nonballistic injuries and can involve superficial soft tissues of the chest wall, lungs and pleura, diaphragm, and mediastinum. Which of the following is true regarding penetrating injury of the diaphragm and oesophagus?
options: CT scan is highly accurate in identifying diaphragmatic injury.
VATS is not indicated in the evaluation of acute penetrating diaphragmatic injury.
Penetrating oesophageal injury is most commonly isolated.
Flexible endoscopy is useful in the acute diagnosis of oesophageal injury.
Most oesophageal injuries should be treated with non-operative wide drainage.

stem: Chondrosarcoma is the most common primary malignant chest wall tumour. Which of the following statements regarding chondrosarcoma is correct?
options: Chondrosarcomas predominantly occur in the posterior part of the chest wall.
Extraosseous chondrosarcomas are much more common.
Ninety percent of chondrosarcomas occur in the ribs.
These tumours occur twice as often in women as in men.
They most frequently are found along the upper five ribs.

stem: Transthoracic needle aspiration (TTNA), also termed percutaneous needle aspiration (PCNA) allows both cytological and histological samples of pulmonary lesions. It can be performed under biplane fluoroscopy or, more frequently, under CT-guidance. Ultrasound can be also used when the lesion is adjacent to the thoracic wall. Which of the following statements regarding TTNA/PCNA is correct?
options: The sensitivity of PCNA ranges from 40% to 60%.
Seeding of the biopsy track with malignant cells is the most frequently reported complication.
Randomized clinical trials directly comparing the accuracy of the TTNA/PCNA versus transbronchial needle aspiration show similar accuracy.
The transbronchial approach has been shown to have a better safety profile compared to TTNA/PCNA.
Haemoptysis occurs in up to 25-30% of cases following TTNA/PCNA.

stem: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has been used for decades to treat diseased oesophageal mucosa in the setting of squamous dysplasia and carcinoma, as well as Barrett's mucosa with dysplasia or neoplasia. Which of the following statements regarding PDT for the treatment of oesophageal tumours is correct?
options: About 10% of patients will develop a stricture after treatment for high-grade dysplasia.
Combination therapy with laser ablation can cause regression in over 90% of patients with low-grade dysplasia.
It is associated with a higher risk of perforation compared to laser ablation.
Early mortality after PDT for malignant oesophageal obstruction exceeds 10%.
PDT produces equivalent results to esophagectomy for high-grade dysplasia.

stem: Castleman disease is a nonclonal lymphoproliferative disorder and one of the more common causes of nonneoplastic lymphadenopathy. Which of the following statements regarding Castleman’s disease is correct?
options: It is a widespread disease resulting in lymph node hyperplasia.
Radiation is highly effective.
The multicentric form is the most common variety.
It can progress to lymphoma.
Patients with the hyaline vascular form usually present with fever and hemolytic anaemia.

stem: The superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS) comprises various symptoms due to occlusion of the SVC. The resulting increased venous pressure in the upper body may cause oedema of the head, neck, and upper extremities, often associated with cyanosis, plethora, and distended subcutaneous vessels. Despite the often striking clinical presentation, SVCS itself is usually not a life-threatening condition. Which of the following statements regarding classification of SVC obstruction is correct?
options: Obstruction of azygos system = type III
Partial obstruction with antegrade flow through azygos system = type II
Near complete to complete obstruction with antegrade flow through azygos vein = type II
Reversal of azygos flow = type IV
Partial obstruction with reversal of azygos flow = type I

stem: Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality. Surgical pulmonary embolectomy, despite having been in existence for over 100 years, is generally regarded as an option of last resort, with expectedly high mortality rates. Which of the following statements regarding the results of surgical intervention for acute pulmonary embolism is correct?
options: Institution of CPR does not affect outcome.
Sepsis is a major cause of death.
Cardiopulmonary bypass reduces operative mortality by 50%.
If thrombolysis is unsuccessful, surgery carries a prohibitive risk.
Recurrent embolization occurs in less than 10% of patients successfully treated with thrombolysis.

stem: Approximately one third of cancer patients are diagnosed with lung metastases making the lungs one of the most common metastatic site. Which of the following is true regarding various metastatic lesions to the lung?
options: A new lung nodule in a breast cancer patient most likely represents a metastatic lesion.
Multiple metastases do not affect prognosis in melanoma.
The most common site of metastasis in renal cell carcinoma is the pleura.
A new lung nodule in a head and neck cancer patient most likely represents a primary lung cancer.
Metastasectomy for renal cell metastasis is rarely indicated.

stem: Thoracic aortic aneurysms tend to be asymptomatic and were previously often diagnosed only after a complication such as dissection or rupture occurred. Better imaging techniques and an increase in the use of cross-sectional imaging has led to an increase in the diagnosis of aortic aneurysms, which has allowed for elective treatment prior to the development of a complication. Which of the following statements regarding aetiology of aortic aneurysm is correct?
options: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is caused by defective synthesis of type II collagen.
Cystic medical degeneration is the most common cause of descending thoracic aneurysms
Development of aneurysms in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is uncommon.
Inflammatory disorders classically produce aneurysms of the proximal descending aorta.

stem: Ascending aortic aneurysms involving the aortic root with diseased valve are usually treated with replacement of the ascending aorta and the aortic valve using a composite valved conduit. Which of the following statements regarding 5-year survival after aortic aneurysm repair is correct?
options: Ascending aorta = 80%
Arch = 80%
Descending aorta = 70%
Thoracoabdominal = 40%
Marfan ascending aorta = 95%

stem: Interstitial lung diseases represent a heterogeneous group of rare respiratory disorders, mostly chronic and associated with high morbidity and mortality. Which of the following is correct regarding patient evaluation for interstitial lung disease?
options: Pulmonary function tests typically demonstrate an obstructive pattern.
Diffusion capacity is usually normal.
The presence of honeycombing on chest CT indicates a worse prognosis.
A single lung biopsy is the most effective method of definitive diagnosis.
Bronchoalveolar lavage is most useful in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

stem: A 53-year-old man with ischaemic cardiomyopathy is being treated with intravenous heparin and dobutamine while awaiting a heart transplant. In the Intensive Care Unit he experiences chest pain, dyspnoea and tachypnoea. Which of the following will provide the most helpful information for this patient’s management?
options: arterial blood gases
chest x-ray
lung scan
right heart catheterisation
12-lead electrocardiogram

stem: A 68-year-old man presented with shortness of breath, fatigue, and limitation in his physical activities. On physical examination, a pansystolic murmur is present. His trans-oesophageal echocardiogram shows mitral regurgitation. Which of the following echocardiographic findings has the highest sensitivity and specificity in prediction of the severity of mitral regurgitation?
options: decrease in pulmonary venous diastolic blood flow
maximal regurgitant area
ratio of the flow jet area to the left atrial area
reversal of pulmonary venous systolic blood flow
size of the left atrium

stem: A 72 year old man underwent an uneventful three-vessel coronary artery bypass operation. Postoperatively, his heart rate is 130 beats per minute, blood pressure is 120/60 mmHg, and temperature is 35.0°C. The FiO2 is 1.0 and he is on 5 cm H2O positive end-expiratory pressure. arterial blood gases: pH = 7.33; pCO2 = 47 mmHg pO2 = 280 mmHg HCO3 = 20 mEq/L O2 sat = 100% hematocrit = 34% pulmonary capillary wedge pressure = 14 mmHg Cardiac index = 2.7 right atrial pressure = 12 mmHg systemic vascular resistance = 1,400 mixed venous O2 saturation = 48% While the patient’s haemodynamic status is satisfactory, the fall in the mixed venous O2 saturation is most likely associated with
options: diminished myocardial oxygen consumption.
hypoventilation.
inadequate myocardial preservation.
increased carbon dioxide production.
vasospasm of the left internal thoracic artery graft.

stem: A healthy 58-year-old female, who underwent an uncomplicated coronary artery bypass procedure four days ago, develops sternal instability without any sign of drainage. She has no fever or leukocytosis. She says that she feels well and she is ambulating without difficulty. The best management of this patient is to
options: begin antibiotics and follow for increasing sternal instability.
confine to bed and limit axial activity until the sternum re-stabilizes.
do a computed tomographic scan to identify substernal air.
perform sternal re-wiring as soon as possible.
re-explore if sternal drainage occurs.

stem: A 54-year-old man with ischaemic cardiomyopathy who is awaiting transplantation is dyspnoeic several hours later he has recurrent haemoptysis. X-rays of the chest show cardiomegaly and vascular congestion. Venous doppler studies show thrombosis of iliofemoral veins. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: heparinisation
ligation of the inferior vena cava (IVC)
percutaneous placement of an IVC filter
thrombolytic therapy
venous thrombectomy

stem: Five months following aortic valve replacement utilizing a bioprosthetic valve, a 68-year-old patient presents with fevers and malaise. Multiple blood cultures are positive for Candida albicans and an echocardiogram shows an 8 mm vegetation on the prosthesis. Proper management is
options: amphotericin B and thrombolytic therapy.
a full course of amphotericin B followed by aortic valve replacement.
a full course of amphotericin B, serial echocardiography and aortic valve replacement if vegetation size increases.
initial amphotericin B followed by serial blood cultures.
aortic valve replacement after starting amphotericin B therapy.

stem: A 76-year-old man with aortic regurgitation and chronic atrial fibrillation requires aortic valve replacement. Which of the following valve replacement options is best for this patient?
options: a stented bioprosthetic valve
a tilting disk valve
homograft composite root replacement
pulmonary autograft (Ross procedure)
bileaflet valve

stem: Recent advances in imaging and staging modalities and improved spatial resolution of computed tomography scan have refined the presentation and diagnosis of early-stage non-small cell lung cancer. Which of the following statements regarding surgery for early-stage lung cancer is correct?
options: Local recurrence after segmentectomy is equivalent to lobectomy.
Lymph node dissection improves survival for stage I tumours.
Tumours greater than 3 cm in diameter have reduced survival compared to smaller tumours.
No adjuvant therapy is required for a stage I tumour following complete resection.
The majority of recurrence after stage I disease is local.

stem: Lobectomy is the gold-standard treatment for early-stage non-small cell lung cancer. Which of the following statements regarding complications after surgery for lung cancer is correct?
options: Major complications occur in less than 5% of patients with stage I disease.
Total morbidity approaches 40% in most series.
Overall mortality for surgical resection is about 5%.
Pneumonectomy has the highest mortality, approximately 20%
Multimodality therapy has been definitively shown to increase complication rates.

stem: The cervical ganglia are paravertebral ganglia of the sympathetic nervous system. Which of the following statements regarding the anatomy of the cervical ganglia is correct?
options: The superior cervical ganglion is a fusion of C1 through C4.
Preganglionic sympathetic outflow to the arm is mostly through C7 and C8.
The middle cervical ganglion combines with the stellate ganglion.
The nerve of Kunz bypasses the superior cervical ganglion.
Cervical ganglionectomy is the preferred technique for denervation of the arm.

stem: The trachea, colloquially called windpipe, is a tube that connects the pharynx and larynx to the lungs, allowing the passage of air. Which of the following statements regarding tracheal anatomy is correct?
options: The average length of the trachea is 20 cm
The last ring above the carina is the only complete ring
The plane between the trachea and the oesophagus is highly vascular
The lower tracheal blood supply arises from intercostal branches
The right recurrent laryngeal nerve is only adjacent to the trachea for a few centimeters at the upper portion.

stem: Brain metastases are not only the most common intracranial neoplasm in adults but also very prevalent in patients with lung cancer. Which of the following statements regarding brain metastases is correct?
options: Less than 25% of patients dying of lung cancer will have brain metastases.
Surgical resection followed by whole brain irradiation improves survival of a solitary brain metastasis.
Multiple brain lesions are best treated by stereotactic radiosurgery.
Five-year survival is less than 10% in surgically treated patients.
Adjuvant corticosteroid therapy has been shown to increase complication rates.

stem: In patients over 50 years of age, neoplasms of the pleura are probably the second most common cause of a pleural effusion after congestive heart failure. Which of the following tumours does not commonly metastasize to the pleural space?
options: Thymoma
Breast carcinoma
Lung carcinoma
Ovarian carcinoma
Prostate carcinoma

stem: The anomalous origin of pulmonary artery from the aorta is a rare but important entity, necessitating a scrupulous preoperative and intraoperative evaluation. Patients presenting this anomaly may undergo correction using various surgical techniques with acceptable results. Which of the following statements regarding operative treatment of anomalous origin of the pulmonary arteries is correct?
options: The anomalous right pulmonary artery should be mobilized and brought in front of the superior vena cava to obtain additional length.
A patch should be placed on the posterior portion of the ascending aorta to avoid stenosis.
A portion of the posterior wall of the ascending aorta can be retained on the right pulmonary artery to achieve greater length.
Late stenosis of the RPA-pulmonary trunk anastomosis should be managed with interposition graft.
Concomitant cardiac anomalies do not increase risk of death

stem: Scimitar syndrome, or pulmonary venolobar syndrome, is a rare congenital anomaly. Which of the following statements regarding the Scimitar syndrome is correct?
options: The anomalous left pulmonary vein curves sharply to the right at the IVC-right atrial junction, giving the classic crescentic shape on radiographs.
Anomalies of the lung are infrequent.
The anomalous vein usually passes anterior to the hilum, through the diaphragm and drains at the confluence of the hepatic veins.
Central and hilar portions of the pulmonary artery are often absent.
Associated anomalies are uncommon.

stem: Atrioventricular septal defect also known as endocardial cushion defect is severe congenital heart disease which is often associated with chromosomal abnormalities or is a part of a malformation syndrome. Which of the following statements regarding clinical manifestations and diagnosis of atrioventricular septal defect is correct?
options: Right-to-left shunting is found in virtually all patients.
Important AV valve regurgitation is present in most patients with partial atrioventricular septal defect.
Patients with complete atrioventricular septal defect typically present in late childhood or early adulthood with progressive cyanosis.
The vectorcardiogram shows a counterclockwise frontal loop.
LV outflow tract obstruction is most common in Rastelli type C morphology.

stem: Treatment options for achalasia include oral pharmacologic therapy, endoscopic injection of botulinum toxin, pneumatic dilation, and myotomy (conventionally by laparoscopy, but more recently by an endoscopic approach). Which of the following is correct regarding treatment of achalasia?
options: Botulinum toxin injection provides good long-lasting palliation.
Pneumatic dilation results in oesophageal perforation in over 10% of patients.
Myotomy and pneumatic dilation produce equivalent mid-term results.
About 10% of patients will have reflux after laparoscopic Heller myotomy.
A 1 cm extension onto the stomach improves outcomes.

stem: An 85-year-old woman who weighs 58 kg presents with severe heart failure. She has critical aortic stenosis and depressed left ventricular function. At operation for aortic valve replacement, she is found to have a small aortic annulus (19 mm). There is a history of gastrointestinal bleeding. Which of the following valve replacement options is best?
options: aortic root enlargement and aortic valve replacement with a 21 mm porcine bioprosthesis.
aortic valve replacement with a 19 mm bileaflet mechanical valve.
aortic valve replacement with a 19 mm bovine pericardial bioprosthesis.
aortic valve replacement with a 19 mm porcine bioprosthesis.
homograft composite aortic root replacement.

stem: The early randomized trials of surgery vs. angioplasty in the treatment of multivessel coronary disease suggested several conclusions. Which of the following is the mostly firmly supported clinical statement from these trials?
options: Angioplasty for patients with multivessel disease may be safely utilized to delay surgical intervention without significantly increasing mortality or major morbidity.
The crossover from angioplasty to surgery in these trials was approximately 20%, but the crossover from surgery to angioplasty was nearly the same.
Even though the early mortality of surgery was higher than angioplasty, by three years the mortality difference between the groups was not significantly different.
Forty to fifty percent of patients in the angioplasty groups had repeat invasive procedures during three years of follow-up.;
Myocardial infarction occurred slightly more frequently in the angioplasty groups, but this difference was not significant.

stem: A 67-year-old patient has three occluded vein grafts and a patent left internal mammary artery (LIMA) graft to a large left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery. Intermittent antegrade/ retrograde cold blood cardioplegia is planned with a systemic temperature of 28°C and clamping of the LIMA graft. During placement of the retrograde coronary sinus catheter, perforation of the coronary sinus occurs. Which of the following strategies is preferable?
options: Cool to 34°C and use antegrade blood cardioplegia via the aorta and vein grafts as completed with the LIMA left open to ensure LAD territory protection. Repair the coronary sinus at the end of the procedure.
Cool to 22°C, infuse antegrade blood cardioplegia via the aorta and down each vein graft as it is completed with the LIMA occluded. Repair the coronary sinus last.
Cool to 22°C, infuse antegrade blood cardioplegia via the aorta and vein grafts as completed with the LIMA open. Repair the coronary sinus last.

Insert the coronary sinus catheter through the perforation into the proximal coronary sinus. Secure the catheter in place with a snare. Proceed with antegrade/retrograde blood cardioplegia and repair the coronary sinus last.

Repair the coronary sinus, advance the catheter beyond the site of perforation and proceed with the operation as planned. The right coronary artery system should be grafted first to facilitate infusion of blood cardioplegia into this region.

stem: A 58-year-old obese, diabetic man who had been debilitated by chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and emphysema from a 40 pack-year smoking history underwent coronary artery bypass grafting with a left internal mammary artery to the left anterior descending coronary artery. Two weeks later he developed severe suppurative mediastinitis with systemic sepsis. At re-exploration the mediastinum was debrided, irrigated, and packed open for frequent dressing changes. He was returned to the intensive care unit on full ventilatory support. Two weeks later during an attempt to wean from the ventilator, he coughed and became hypotensive with dark bleeding becoming obvious through the dressings. His blood pressure was stabilized with intravenous fluid infusions. Preferred emergent therapy should be
options: haemorrhage control alone.
haemorrhage control and muscle flap closure.
haemorrhage control and re-packing the mediastinum.
haemorrhage control and secure sternal closure over irrigation catheters.
haemorrhage control and secure sternal re-closure.

stem: A patient with normal preoperative ventricular function underwent coronary artery bypass grafting to the left anterior descending and circumflex marginal coronary arteries. Trans-oesophageal echocardiography (TEE) reveals severe mitral valve insufficiency, an akinetic infero-lateral wall, and depressed left ventricular function. The most prudent course of action is to
options: add vasopressor medication in large doses.
insert an intra-aortic balloon pump or left ventricular assist device.
re-evaluate and/or re-graft the circumflex marginal system.
replace or repair the mitral valve.
rest the heart on cardiopulmonary bypass and repeat the TEE in 30 minutes.

stem: A 62-year-old man requires three vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Which of the following co-morbidities is associated with the highest risk of mortality from CABG?
options: ejection fraction less than 20%
myocardial infarction within six hours of operation
preoperative intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation required to support blood pressure
previous open heart procedure
renal failure requiring dialysis

stem: You are called to the cardiac catheterisation laboratory to evaluate a 72 years old man in the midst of an angioplasty. Prior to angioplasty, the patient had a total occlusion of the proximal circumflex coronary artery and a 70% stenosis of the right coronary artery (RCA). While the cardiologist was attempting to open the circumflex coronary artery, the patient developed pulmonary oedema and hypotension. Blood pressure is now 90/60 mmHg on low-dose dopamine and the pulse oximeter reads 93% (40% oxygen mask). A possible dissection at the origin of the circumflex coronary artery is visible. Your recommendation should be
options: emergency institution of percutaneous femoral cardiopulmonary bypass to support the patient while the circumflex coronary artery is opened and a stent is used in the area of possible dissection. The RCA should be left for another day.
emergency operation preceded by placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump. The left internal mammary graft should be placed to the circumflex system and a vein graft to the RCA.
emergency operation preceded by placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump. Vein grafts should be performed to the circumflex system and to the RCA.
emergency operation with rapid institution of cardiopulmonary bypass and vein grafts to the circumflex and right systems and a mammary graft to the left anterior descending coronary artery.

emergency placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump and intravenous heparin for three days to allow resolution of pulmonary oedema and return of normal pulmonary capillary function followed by coronary artery bypass.

stem: The most common early complication after heart-lung transplantation for patients with Eisenmenger’s syndrome is
options: hypoxia.
mediastinal haemorrhage.
stroke.
tracheal anastomotic dehiscence.
ventricular arrhythmia.

stem: A 41 year old diabetic dialysis-dependent man presented with fever (39.5°C) and chills. Two positive blood cultures revealed Xanthomonas maltophilia (gram-negative). Six days after starting sensitivity-directed intravenous antibiotics, he developed severe dyspnea and a grade VI diastolic murmur along the left sternal border. The transoesophageal echocardiogram shows severe aortic insufficiency with an aortic root abscess which extends into the mitral valve annulus and mitral anterior leaflet. There is near aorto-ventricular discontinuity. The best therapy for this patient is
options: antibiotic therapy for six weeks followed by aortic valve replacement (St. Jude).
antibiotic therapy and dialysis for congestive heart failure.
antibiotic therapy initiation, homograft aortic root replacement and mitral valve repair
aortic valve replacement (St. Jude) with patch repair of the aortic root.
mitral valve repair with autologous pericardium.

stem: Ten years ago a 52-year-old man, who now is in congestive heart failure, had an emergency mitral valve replacement with a bioprosthesis and a three-vessel coronary bypass operation after a myocardial infarction. Coronary angiography now demonstrates a patent right internal mammary artery graft to the left anterior descending coronary artery, a patent left internal mammary graft to the circumflex marginal coronary artery, and a non-diseased patent vein graft to the posterior descending coronary artery. He has severe mitral valve insufficiency. The safest approach for reoperative mitral valve replacement is
options: left lateral thoracotomy, deep hypothermia and retrograde cardioplegia.
median sternotomy and antegrade cardioplegia.
median sternotomy, hypothermia and ventricular fibrillation.
right anterolateral thoracotomy, hypothermia and ventricular fibrillation.
right anterolateral thoracotomy, mild hypothermia and antegrade cardioplegia.

stem: Congenital aortic valve stenosis is a common lesion, with an approximate incidence of 5 to 7% of all cardiac malformations and occupies the first place among left heart obstructions. Which of the following statements regarding congenital aortic valve stenosis is correct?
options: Calcification is often present before age 20.
Calcification occurs earlier in women.
The process is maximal at sites of commissural fusion.
Complete heart block can occur from extension of calcification below the right coronary cusp.
Ross procedure has early mortality rates of more than 5%.

stem: Rheumatic heart disease is well known to be an active inflammatory process which develops progressive calcification and leaflet thickening over time. Which of the following statements regarding rheumatic aortic stenosis is correct?
options: It is characterized by fusion of all three commissures to some degree.
Calcification is most prominent at the commissures.
It is usually an isolated process.
The majority of patients will have a remote history of rheumatic fever.
The Ross procedure has similar autograft reoperation rates in rheumatic and non-rheumatic aortic valve disease.

stem: During a fight a man is stabbed in the lateral chest beneath the right arm. The wound does not enter the chest cavity. Physical examination reveals that the vertebral (medial) border of the patient's scapula projects posteriorly and is closer to the midline on the injured side. On return visit the patient complains that he cannot reach as far forward (such as to reach for a door knob) as he could before the injury. The nerve injured which caused these symptoms is the
options: axillary nerve
long thoracic nerve
musculocutaneous nerve
radial nerve
suprascapular nerve

stem: In a post-football match brawl, a 38-year-old man was stabbed in the back with a knife that just nicked his left lung halfway between its apex and diaphragmatic surface. Which part of the lung was most likely injured?
options: Hilum
Inferior lobe
Lingula
Middle lobe
Superior lobe

stem: A 48-year-old man died of immediate respiratory failure due to a self-inflicted gunshot wound injuring his brainstem. Which of the following statements accurately describes the interaction of respiratory centers in the brainstem and their effect on respiration?
options: The medullary rhythmicity center is a discrete group of neurons whose rhythmicity is abolished when the brain is transected above and below this area.
Sectioning the brainstem above the pons, near the inferior colliculus of the midbrain results in immediate respiratory arrest.
Transection above the apneustic center results in prolonged expiration and very short inspiration.
Transection of the afferent fibers of the vagus and glossopharyngeal nerves results in prolonged inspiration and shortened expiration.
The apneustic and pneumotaxic center of the pons are essential for maintenance of the basic rhythm of respiration.

stem: Which of the following congenital cardiac lesions is most frequently inoperable in the adult age group due to the development of pulmonary vascular obstructive disease?
options: atrial septal defect
atrioventricular septal defect
pulmonary stenosis
tetralogy of Fallot
ventricular septal defect

stem: Exposure of the aortic arch for repair of arch aneurysm usually requires
options: combined median sternotomy and left interspace incision.
division and oversewing of the divided ends of the innominate vein.
extended left neck incision.
left thoracotomy.
median sternotomy.

stem: A 71 year old man with undiagnosed hypertension and previous history of blunt thoracic trauma presented with progressive hoarseness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed large, medially oriented false aneurysm just beyond the left subclavian artery. Which of the following statements is true?
options: The artery of Adamkiewicz arises between T5 and T8 in 75% of patients.
Clamping the left subclavian artery, as well as the thoracic aorta just beyond the subclavian, significantly increases the risk of paraplegia.
Decreased intraspinal pressure increases the probability of paraplegia.
During cross-clamping just beyond the left subclavian artery the temperature of the cord is unrelated to the likelihood of paraplegia.
The risk of paraplegia is approximately 50% if the aorta is clamped just beyond the subclavian artery for 60 minutes (“Clamp and go”).

stem: In the “elephant trunk” operation,
options: the distal anastomosis is made to the distal end of the Dacron graft.
the distal segment or “elephant trunk” should always be longer than 10 cm.
the graft is invaginated on itself for performance of the distal anastomosis.
moderate hypothermia is usually sufficient.
the operation is ordinarily completed in a single stage.

stem: Congenital malformations of the mitral valve may be encountered in isolation or in association with other congenital heart defects. Each level of the mitral valve complex may be affected, according to the embryological development, explaining the fact that these lesions are sometimes associated with each other. Which of the following statements regarding morphology of congenital mitral valve disease is correct?
options: Usually the congenital defect affects the anterior leaflet.
A supravalvar ring may cause death after repair of tetralogy of Fallot.
Patients with congenital mitral regurgitation have more severe coexisting cardiac anomalies than patients with congenital mitral stenosis.
A parachute valve typically causes isolated severe regurgitation.
Absence of commissural leaflet tissue results in compensatory mitral stenosis.

stem: Tracheal tumours are rare and account for only 2% of all respiratory tract tumours. Which of the following statement regarding tracheal pathology is correct?
options: Most primary tracheal tumours are benign.
Squamous cell carcinoma occurs primarily in smokers.
Lymph node metastases are more common in adenoid cystic carcinoma.
Submucosal spread is a typical feature of squamous cell carcinoma.
Thyroid carcinomas typically invade the trachea at the level of the cricoid cartilage.

stem: Surgical resection of the trachea and carina requires a highly specialized team of thoracic surgeons, anesthesiologists, and operative support staff because of the complex nature of these procedures. Which of the following statements regarding tracheal resection is true?
options: A partial upper sternal split is the best approach for most upper tracheal lesions.
The perivascular fascia and mediastinal fat should be widely resected as part of the lymph node dissection.
Sutures should be placed through the cartilaginous rings to prevent dehiscence
Tissue flaps should be used to cover the anastomosis in an irradiated field.
The recurrent laryngeal nerve should be carefully dissected free from tumour involvement.

stem: Traumatic diaphragmatic injury is a not uncommon accompaniment to blunt or penetrating trauma to the abdomen or thorax. Which is true regarding blunt diaphragmatic injury?
options: Frontal impact is more likely to result in diaphragm rupture than lateral impact.
The site of rupture is on the left side in about 2/3 of patients.
Most patients will develop symptoms of obstruction within 3 years if the initial rupture goes undetected.
Diagnostic peritoneal lavage is highly specific.
Thoracotomy is the preferred approach for repair of acute rupture.

stem: Tracheobronchial injuries are rare but potentially life-threatening injuries. They comprise injuries that occur between the cricoid cartilage and right and left main-stem tracheal bifurcation. Which of the following statements regarding blunt tracheobronchial injuries is correct?
options: Most are due to motor vehicle accidents.
The majority occur in the peripheral bronchi.
The most common diagnostic sign is haemoptysis
A left mainstem bronchus injury is best approached through the left chest
The “dashboard” injury results in avulsion of both mainstem bronchi
