stem: Thoracoscopic sympathectomy is effective and safe treatment for severe palmar, axillary, and craniofacial hyperhidrosis. Which of the following statements regarding outcomes after surgical treatment of hyperhidrosis is correct?
options: Recurrence rates for palmar hyperhidrosis are about 10%.
Treatment of craniofacial hyperhidrosis is less successful than for palmar hyperhidrosis.
Horner’s syndrome occurs in 3-4% of patients and usually resolves.
Compensatory sweating occurs in about 25% of patients.
The cardiorespiratory response to exercise may be diminished.

stem: Pulmonary metastasectomy represents an established approach in the treatment of lung metastases related to several solid malignant tumours, promising the chance of long term survival. Which of the following does not have a high predilection for pulmonary metastasis?
options: Testicular tumours
Melanoma
Glioblastoma multiforme
Kaposi’s sarcoma
Ewing’s sarcoma

stem: During aortic arch and cerebrovascular surgery, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest affords the brain some measure of protection by reducing cellular metabolic rate, excitatory transmitter release and generation of free radicals, vascular permeability, blood-brain barrier disruption, and postischaemic cerebral oedema. D Which of the following statements regarding deep hypothermic circulatory arrest is correct?
options: Core body temperatures of 18 °C to 20 °C are safe for periods as long as 90 to 120 minutes.
The coagulopathy induced by hypothermia and circulatory stasis is mainly caused by kinin/kallikrein perturbations.
Near infra-red spectroscopy (NIRS) is an invasive monitoring technique that measures regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rSO2) during deep hypothermic circulatory arrest.
In brain tissue, the vascular compartment is predominantly venous.
Levels of rSO2 of <65% are indicative of neurologic compromise.

stem: The phrenic nerves arise from the neck (C3-C5) and innervate the diaphragm. The phrenic nerves course over which muscle in the neck?
options: Anterior scalene muscles
Middle scalene muscles
Posterior scalene muscles
Sternocleidomastoid muscles
Trapezius muscles

stem: A 23-year-old woman in severe respiratory distress is scheduled to undergo an open lung biopsy. Her serology is positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). In order to prevent virus transmission and maximize protection in the intensive care unit the members of the surgical team should
options: take azidothymidine (AZT) single dose immediately after the operation.
take AZT for six weeks after the operation.
undergo periodic serologic testing for HIV exposure.
wear gloves when touching mucous membranes or non-intact skin.
wear masks and gloves when in contact with the patient.

stem:
Lung compliance in a 32-year-old woman is studied. Data collected under control and experimental conditions are listed in the following table.
Control: respiratory rate 15 breaths/min; tidal volume 600 ml; change in interpleural pressure during inspiration 4 cm H2O.
Experimental: respiratory rate 25 breaths/min; tidal volume 600 ml; change in interpleural pressure during inspiration 10 cm H2O.
This patient’s lung compliance during control and experimental conditions was
options: unchanged
40 ml/breath and 24 ml/breath, respectively
150 ml/cm H2O and 60 ml/cm H2O, respectively
150 cm H2O/ml and 60 cm H2O/ml, respectively
500 ml/cm H2O

stem: A lightly anaesthetised man who is breathing spontaneously has a cardiac output of 6 L/min, a heart rate of 75 beats/min, an O2 consumption of 240 ml/min, and a mixed venous O2 tension of 40 mm Hg. He is ventilated for 10 minutes at his normal tidal volume but at twice the normal frequency with a gas mixture that is 20% O2 and 80% N2. The airway pressure at the end of inspiration is 5 cm H2O. On cessation of artificial ventilation, the patient does not breathe for 1 minute. During the artificial ventilation, the mixed venous O2 tension in this patient would be
options: equal to 40 mm Hg because the metabolic rate was unchanged
greater than 40 mm Hg because the hyperventilation would cause vasoconstriction and less gas exchange with the tissues
greater than 40 mm Hg because of the significant increase in P50 of hemoglobin
less than 40 mm Hg because of the hypoxia that would occur from breathing this gas mixture
less than 40 mm Hg because of a decrease in cardiac output

stem: A patient presents with crushing chest pain, shortness of breath, and marked anxiety. A preliminary diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction is made. Physical examination reveals evidence of pulmonary edema, cardiomegaly, peripheral edema, and pulmonary hypertension. Arterial blood gas analysis, on room air, reveals the following: Pco2 = 40 mm Hg, Po2 = 60 mm Hg, pH = 7.32, and [HCO3−] = 20 mEq/L This patient’s blood data are most indicative of
options: a diffusion abnormality
hypoventilation
a ventilation-perfusion abnormality
left-to-right cardiac shunt
right-to-left cardiac shunt

stem: Caustic ingestion continues to be a significant problem world-wide especially in developing countries. Which of the following statements regarding management of caustic injury of the oesophagus is correct?
options: Liquid alkali produces the most injury at points of narrowing.
First-degree injury consists of mucosal blistering.
Pseudomembranes are seen in third-degree injury.
Early dilation is important to prevent stricture formation.
Emesis should be induced in alkali poisoning.

stem: Schatzki's ring is a benign cause of dysphagia in adults. Which of the following statements regarding Schatzki’s ring is correct?
options: It occurs below the squamocolumnar junction
The ring is formed by fibrous replacement of the mucosa
There is no association with hiatal hernia
The narrowing can be successfully treated with dilation
Endoscopy is the diagnostic method of choice

stem: Leiomyomas cause symptoms due to partial obstruction of the oesophageal lumen, leading to the diagnosis and subsequent treatment. Which of the following is correct concerning oesophageal leiomyoma?
options: They account for less than 20% of all benign oesophageal tumours.
Most arise from the submucosa.
Distal tumours are associated with GORD.
Endoscopic biopsy is the diagnostic procedure of choice.
Malignant transformation is common.

stem: The aorta, which has a complex intrinsic biology and sophisticated mechanical properties for conducting the blood ejected from the left ventricle to the rest of the systemic arterial bed, is the largest and strongest artery in the body. Which of the following statements regarding aetiology of aortic dissection is correct?
options: More than 50% of patients exhibit some degree of cystic medial necrosis.
Acute dissection occurs in less than 20% of patients with Marfan syndrome.
Nearly all patients with Marfan syndrome and acute dissection also have cystic medial necrosis.
Cusp resuspension is discouraged in anuloaortic ectasia.
Patients with coarctation and dissection have degenerative changes of the aortic wall.

stem: Benign tumours and tumour-like conditions of the lung are encountered in the pathologic evaluation of asymptomatic and symptomatic lung nodules. Since many of these lesions are uncommon, they can be diagnostically challenging. Which of the following statements regarding various benign lung tumours is correct?
options: Mucous gland adenomas usually occur on the left side.
Intrapulmonary fibrous tumours originate from the bronchus.
Fibrous histiocytomas are ideally treated with endobronchial resection.
Granular cell tumours arise from skeletal muscle.
Plasma cell granulomas are the most common lung lesion in older children.

stem: Following an aortic valve replacement for aortic stenosis, an 80 year old woman was returned to the intensive care unit. Her initial vital signs and haemodynamic data include: Pulse: 115 beats per minute Pulmonary artery pressure: 50/30 mmHg Blood pressure: 90/40 mmHg Pulmonary wedge pressure: 22 mmHg Cardiac index: 1.6 L/[min*m2] Central venous pressure: 25 mmHg Systemic vascular resistance index: 2000 dynes sec cm-5/m3 The most appropriate management for this patient is
options: a 250cc bolus of fluid.
dobutamine at 5.0 mcg/[kg*min].
furosemide 20 mg intravenously.
isoprenaline at 0.05 mcg/[kg*min].
noradrenaline at 0.05 mcg/[kg*min].

stem: A 65 years old woman had an aortic valve replacement seven days ago. Her rhythm strip is shown. She has normal sinus node function. The most appropriate pacing mode for this patient is
options: AAI.
AAO.
DDD.
VVI.
VVIR.

stem: A 67 years old woman experienced syncope five days after undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery. She is also recovering from an inferior wall infarction. A rhythm strip is shown. Immediate management should consist of
options: insertion of a temporary pacemaker.
intravenous atropine.
intravenous lidocaine.
intravenous verapamil.
permanent pacing.

stem: While in the ICU, a 56 years old woman has sudden loss of consciousness eight hours after myocardial revascularization and resection of a ventricular aneurysm. The arterial pressure is 75/40 mmHg. Electrocardiogram (shown) reveals a regular rhythm at a rate of 140 to 200 beats per minute. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: atrial flutter
atrioventricular nodal premature beats
multifocal atrial tachycardia
ventricular parasystole
ventricular tachycardia

stem: A 56 years old man experiences premature ventricular beats 48 hours after undergoing emergency coronary artery surgery and sustaining a myocardial infarction. Immediate suppressive therapy is indicated if these are
options: associated with a non-Q-wave infarction.
associated with a transmural infarction.
in close proximity to the T wave.
more frequent than five per minute.
multifocal.

stem: The rationale for patch plasty techniques in left ventricular aneurysmectomy is to
options: decrease the incidence of post-repair ventricular arrhythmias.
decrease the risk of late false aneurysm formation.
decrease the need for permanent pacemaker.
increase resting cardiac output.
restore the normal curvatures of the ventricular wall.

stem: Atrial septal defects are the third most common type of congenital heart disease. Included in this group of malformations are several types of atrial communications that allow shunting of blood between the systemic and the pulmonary circulations. Which of the following definitions of atrial septal defect is accurate?
options: A large, low ASD that is confluent with the inferior vena cava is termed an ostium primum defect
An oval shaped defect with anterior displacement of the posterior limbus is termed a posterior defect
A sinus venosus ASD is usually associated with anomalous drainage of the right inferior pulmonary vein
Unroofed coronary sinus syndrome typically presents as a fenestration in the midportion of the coronary sinus
Atrioventricular septal defect constitutes absence of the fossa ovalis combined with a ventricular septal defect

stem: Atrial septal defect is a common congenital abnormality that occurs in the form of ostium secundum, ostium primum, sinus venosus, and rarely, coronary sinus defects. Which of the following is true regarding the diagnosis of atrial septal defect?
options: Signs and symptoms are rarely present if the Qp/Qs is less than 1.5.
Palpitations are a classic early symptom.
ECG shows a pattern of counterclockwise frontal loop and incomplete right bundle branch block.
Cardiac catheterization is rarely required.
A large shunt can be detected by a presence of a pulmonary diastolic flow murmur.

stem: A patient with ventricular fibrillation is resuscitated and now shows shortened, irregular QT intervals on his ECG. Which of the following ion channels is responsible for the plateau phase of the cardiac action potential that is reflected by the QT interval?
options: K+ channels
Na+ channels
L-type Ca2+ channels
T-type Ca2+ channels
Cl− channels

stem: A 33-year-old female with congenital aortic stenosis is in her second month of pregnancy. In order to evaluate the potential risk this pregnancy poses to her, she is admitted for cardiac function testing. O2 consumption (measured by analysis of mixed expired gas) in this patient is 300 mL/min, arterial O2 content is 20 mL/100 mL blood, pulmonary arterial O2 content is 15 mL/100 mL blood, and her heart rate is 60/min. Her cardiac stroke volume is
options: 1 mL
10 mL
60 mL
100 mL
200 mL

stem: A patient on intensive care is ventilated with a frequency of 12 per minute and a tidal volume of 0.6 liters. His arterial pH increases to > 7.6. In order to correct this respiratory alkalosis, you should
options: increase oxygen fraction
increase minute ventilation
decrease dead space
decrease tidal volume
use positive end expiratory pressure (PEEP)

stem: The cardiac cycle is the sequence of events that occurs when the heart beats. In the cardiac cycle, the period of isometric contraction occurs
options: During the second heart sound
During the P wave of the electrocardiogram
During the maximum ventricular ejection
With the aortic valve closed
With the aortic valve open

stem: The first rib is the most superior of the twelve ribs. It is an important anatomical landmark and is one of the borders of the superior thoracic aperture. Which of the following statements regarding the first rib is correct?
options: It is a typical rib.
The groove for the subclavian artery contains the lowest lowest brachial plexus trunk as well as the subclavian artery.
The groove for the subclavian vein is posterior to the scalene tubercle.
The costal groove on its inferior surface contains intercostals vessels and nerves.
The middle scalene muscle inserts on the scalene tubercle.

stem: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) or degenerative aortic stenosis is the most common valvular heart disease in the elderly. As life expectancy increases, prevalence of CAVD is expected to rise. Which of the following statements regarding degenerative aortic stenosis is correct?
options: There is no commissural fusion.
There is no association with atherosclerosis.
The calcification is usually isolated to the valve leaflets.
Associated mitral calcification is uncommon.
It is characterized by progressive metastatic calcification of aortic cusps.

stem: Aortic coarctation represents a distinct anatomic obstruction as blood moves from the ascending to the descending aorta and can present in a range of ages from infancy to adulthood. Which of the following statements regarding morphology of coarctation of the aorta is correct?
options: It is produced by infolding of the aortic intima.
It is more common when there is reduced ductal flow in utero.
The aortic wall beyond the coarctation is usually thin and dilated.
There is often concomitant narrowing of the aortic isthmus.
Excessive antegrade flow through the first and second intercostals arteries results in rib notching.

stem: Coronary arteriovenous fistulae are abnormal communications between a coronary artery and a cardiac chamber or major vessel (vena cava, pulmonary veins, pulmonary artery). Which of the following statements regarding clinical manifestations and natural history of coronary arteriovenous fistulae is correct?
options: Most present in infancy or early childhood as asymptomatic murmurs.
When symptomatic, the most common complaint is angina.
Heart failure is uncommon but typically occurs in infants or young children.
Rupture is common, particularly with left-sided fistulae.
Spontaneous closure is rare.

stem: The epidemiology of infective endocarditis is changing due to a number of factors, including more frequent and varied antibiotic use, the emergence of resistant microorganisms, and an increase in the implantation of cardiovascular devices. Which of the following statements regarding the morphology of endocarditis is correct?
options: Vegetations typically occur on the aortic side of the aortic valve leaflets.
Most cases of native valve endocarditis affect left-sided valves.
Only 25% of intravenous drug use related cases affect the tricuspid valve.
Streptococcus viridans is the most common organism associated with periannular abscess.
Most vegetations occur on the atrial side of a mitral prosthesis.

stem: Ischaemic mitral regurgitation is a common complication of left ventricular (LV) dysfunction related to chronic coronary artery disease. This complex multifactorial disease involves global and regional LV remodeling, as well as dysfunction and distortion of the components of the mitral valve including the chordae, the annulus, and the leaflets. Which of the following statements regarding morphology of mitral regurgitation from ischaemic heart disease is correct?
options: More than 75% have complete rupture of at least one papillary muscle in acute mitral insufficiency.
The anterolateral papillary muscle is the most commonly ruptured.
Moderate or severe mitral regurgitation in the setting of acute myocardial infarction is a predictor of mortality.
Less than 25% of patients with chronic mitral insufficiency and ischaemic heart disease also have concomitant myxomatous degeneration..
Chronic mitral regurgitation from ischaemic heart disease usually results in a posteriorly directed jet due to ischaemic contracture of the anterior chordae.

stem: The normal tricuspid valve anatomy and function have several dissimilarities to the corresponding mitral valve in the left heart, in part, based on lower pressures in the right heart chambers. Which of the following statements regarding the pathogenesis of tricuspid valve disease is correct?
options: The septal leaflet has the greatest amount of lengthening during right ventricular dilation.
Isolated rheumatic tricuspid disease usually present as pure stenosis.
The most common organism isolated in tricuspid endocarditis is S. aureus.
Nonpenetrating rupture of a tricuspid papillary muscle usually results in flail of the anterior leaflet.
Tricuspid stenosis is the most common cardiac manifestation of carcinoid syndrome.

stem: Carcinoid heart disease is a rare form of valvular heart disease. The management of these patients is complex, as the systemic malignant disease and the cardiac involvement have to be considered at the same time. Which of the following statements regarding carcinoid heart disease is correct?
options: Up to 90% of patients with carcinoid syndrome present with carcinoid heart disease at diagnosis.
Left-sided cardiac involvement occurs in 50% of patients.
Increased mobility of tricuspid valve leaflets is a pathognomonic echocardiographic feature.
Valve repair is the therapeutic intervention of choice.
Surgical mortality is < 10%.

stem: The photo below shows surgical specimen of excised solitary fibrous tumour of pleura (SFTP). Which of the following statements regarding SFTP is correct?
options: SFTP have a male predominance.
SFTP occur in all age groups.
The majority of them arise from the parietal pleura
Less than 5% of patients present with refractory hyperglycaemia.
There is a strong correlation with genetic predisposition for the tumour.

stem: Neuroendocrine tumours of the lung represent a wide spectrum of phenotypically distinct entities with different biological characteristics such as typical carcinoid tumour (TC), atypical carcinoid tumour (AC), large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC), and small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC). Which of the following statements regarding neuroendocrine tumours of the lung is correct?
options: Patients with atypical carcinoids are more frequently women.
LCNEC is defined as a well differentiated and low-grade neuroendocrine tumour that morphologically is between typical carcinoid and SCLC.
Carcinoid tumours have high numbers of somatostatin receptors.
About 50% carcinoids occur in the peripheral lung
LCNEC has a prevalence of 20% among pulmonary neuroendocrine tumours.

stem: Airway complications after lung transplantation present a formidable challenge to the lung transplant team, ranging from mere unusual images to fatal events. The exact incidence of complications is wide-ranging depending on the type of event, and there is still evolution of a universal characterization of the airway findings. Airway anastomotic complications are least likely following
options: bilateral lung transplant with bilateral (split) omental wrap.
bilateral lung transplant without omental wrap.
double lung transplant with tracheal anastomosis.
heart-lung transplant.
single lung transplant.

stem: Marfan syndrome is a relatively common autosomal dominant hereditary disorder of connective tissue. Which of the following statements concerning Marfan syndrome is correct?
options: The aneurysmal process rarely stops proximal to the innominate artery.
Annulo-aortic ectasia is rare.
Required aortic valve prosthesis sizes are not substantially larger than those used for patients with other valvular lesions.
Subclinical aortic dissection can occur.
Surgery should be performed when the diameter of the proximal aorta exceeds 4 cm in patients with ascending aortic aneurysm, aortic valve incompetence and family history of sudden death.

stem: A 25-year-old woman underwent mitral valve reconstruction for mitral regurgitation due to ruptured posterior leaflet chordae; preoperative left ventricular function was normal and the coronary arteries were normal. Reconstruction consisted of quadrangular leaflet resection, annular plication and leaflet suture, and insertion of a rigid annuloplasty ring. The patient was weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass with difficulty. Haemodynamic measurements post-bypass are: aortic pressure 80/45 mmHg, left ventricular pressure measured by direct needle puncture 130/22 mmHg, cardiac index 1.8 l/[min*m2]. An intraoperative transesophageal echo-cardiogram suggests systolic anterior motion. Proper management is
options: milrinone infusion.
aortic valve replacement.
dobutamine infusion.
mitral valve replacement.
revision of the valvuloplasty.

stem: Beta oxidation of fatty acids takes place in the mitochondrial matrix for the most part. Transfer of acetylated fatty acids from the cytosol to the mitochondria for subsequent beta oxidation requires the presence of adequate levels of
options: carnitine.
coenzyme Q.
creatine phosphokinase.
glutamate.
phospholipase C.

stem: An 80 years old diabetic woman with a degenerated mitral valve and an ejection fraction of 0.35 is undergoing cardiac surgery. There are two ruptured chordae tendineae along the mid-portion of the posterior leaflet and three redundant chords along the mid anterior leaflet. The best option is to
options: excise the anterior and posterior leaflets and insert a bioprosthesis.
excise the posterior leaflet and insert a bioprosthesis.
excise the valve completely and insert a bioprosthesis.
perform a posterior leaflet quadrangular resection and shorten the anterior chords.
preserve both leaflets and insert a bioprosthesis.

stem: Orthotopic cardiac transplantation is contraindicated by
options: age >60 years.
fixed pulmonary vascular resistance >6 Wood units.
a left-sided superior vena cava.
mechanical device support for more than six weeks.
plasma reactive antibodies (PRA) >90%.

stem: A 74 years old man with a history of ventricular tachycardia presents with a two month of malaise. He has had intermittent low grade fevers. Evaluation by his local general physician is unrevealing. Five years ago he had a thoracotomy to implant a cardioverter-defibrillator after failure of amiodarone therapy. He has chronic atrial fibrillation. Ten years ago a VVIR pacemaker system was placed and pacemaker generator was replaced at the time of the ICD generator change 15 months. The ventricle is currently 100% paced. His physical examination is unremarkable on presentation. White cell count is 11,800/mm3 and erythrocyte sedimentation rate = 90 mm/hr. Chest x-ray shows good placement of the endocardial lead, extrapericardial patch, rate-sensing electrode and pulmonary infiltrates. Blood cultures are obtained. The appropriate therapeutic course is
options: commencement of intravenous antibiotic therapy.
commencement of oral antibiotic therapy.
continued observation.
placement of a temporary pacemaker and removal of all hardware (pacemaker and ICD)
placement of a temporary pacemaker and removal of the permanent pacemaker system only.

stem: A debilitated adult patient presents with high fevers, leukocytosis, a pulmonary infiltrate, and large multi-loculated pericardial effusion. On echocardiography, the pericardium is not thickened. A sample of pericardial fluid obtained by pericardiocentesis is turbid; gram stain shows multiple polymorphonuclear leukocytes and gram positive cocci in chains. Culture positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae. Proper management is
options: antibiotic therapy and a pericardial window performed through a left thoracotomy.
antibiotic therapy and subxiphoid placement of a pericardiostomy tube.
antibiotic therapy and a wide pericardial resection through a median sternotomy.
antibiotic therapy, percutaneous drainage, and antibiotic irrigation.
bacteriocidal antibiotic therapy.

stem: A 59 years old man with a history of hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, and good biventricular function underwent coronary bypass grafting for severe three-vessel disease involving left main coronary artery stenosis. One year following surgery, he presented with symptoms of severe biventricular failure. Despite diuretic therapy, symptoms progressed. A thallium test was negative. Cardiac catheterization demonstrates elevated and equalized right and left ventricular diastolic pressures. The next step in management is
options: afterload reduction medication.
bypass graft angiography.
mitral valve replacement.
pericardiectomy.
tricuspid valve replacement.

stem: A 75 years old man presented with unstable angina which was controlled with intravenous heparin and nitroglycerin. Cardiac catheterization documented three-vessel coronary artery disease with a reduced ejection fraction. Surgical revascularization was scheduled. Twelve hours prior to the operation, the heparin was discontinued. On the morning of operation, baseline laboratory values included: platelet count 340,000/mm3 activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) 38 seconds activated clotting time (ACT) 124 seconds Prior to the commencement of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), heparin was given at a dose of 300 U/kg. Three minutes later, an ACT was measured at 200 seconds. A second dose of heparin from another bottle was given directly into the right atrium. The ACT increased to 290 seconds. The most appropriate next step is to
options: accept an ACT of 290 seconds and proceed with CPB.
determine heparin concentration and if greater than 2 U/ml, proceed with CPB.
determine the aPTT, and if twice baseline, proceed with CPB.
give additional heparin until the ACT is greater than 400 seconds.
give fresh frozen plasma and repeat the ACT.

stem: A 78 years old woman with long-standing rheumatic mitral stenosis, secondary moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and severe pulmonary hypertension (85% of systemic pressure) underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve ring annuloplasty. Despite inotropic support with high-dose dopamine and milrinone, the patient is weaned from bypass with the following haemodynamic parameters: arterial blood pressure 75/40 mmHg cardiac index 1.6 L/[min*m2] pulmonary artery pressure 70/50 mmHg left atrial pressure 4 mmHg central venous pressure 24 mmHg Transesophageal echocardiography shows normal left ventricular function and good prosthetic valve function without paravalvular leak. The right ventricle is dilated and there is mild tricuspid regurgitation. There is no air in the heart. Correct management is
options: addition of epinephrine via a central venous line.
addition of isoproterenol via a central venous line.
creation of a small atrial septal defect.
nitric oxide inhalation.
tricuspid valve replacement.

stem: A 45 years old man is studied and found to have a respiratory rate of 15 breaths/min, a tidal volume of 0.5 L, and a dead space of 200 ml. The patient is asked to increase his respiratory rate to 30 breaths/min, and his tidal volume is measured at 350 ml. Assuming no change in dead space, which of the following is correct regarding alveolar CO2 tension?
options: The alveolar CO2 tension will increase because of the decreased ventilation.
The alveolar CO2 tension will decrease because of the increased ventilation.
The alveolar CO2 tension will not change because it is not affected by respiration.
The alveolar CO2 tension will not change because alveolar ventilation remains constant.
The arterial blood pH will decrease because of the increased ventilation.

stem: A 42 years old man who was involved in a head-on motor vehicle accident underwent total body CT scan that clearly indicates an innominate artery tear. The correct surgical approach for this injury is
options: “clam-shell” incision.
left thoracotomy.
median sternotomy.
right thoracotomy.
“trap-door” incision.

stem: Blunt cardiac injury is common and may cause significant morbidity and mortality. In blunt cardiac rupture
options: the atria are the most frequent sites of injury.
median sternotomy and cardiopulmonary bypass are usually required for repair.
signs of external thoracic trauma are always present.
survival is highest with ventricular injuries.
upper torso and neck cyanosis is a key physical finding.

stem: A 21 years old carpenter impales on a long nail that penetrated his chest. On arrival in A&E he is alert, with a blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg, a pulse of 110 beats per minute, and a respiratory rate of 24 breaths per minute. The nail moves with each heart beat. Which of the following is the best treatment for this patient?
options: pericardiocentesis and withdrawal of the nail
thoracotomy to remove the nail
withdrawal of the nail followed by pericardiocentesis
withdrawal of the nail and injection of radiopaque dye into the tract
withdrawal of the nail and observation

stem: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is the most common lesion of the tricuspid valve. Mild TR is common and usually is benign. However, moderate or severe TR can lead to irreversible myocardial damage and adverse outcomes. The most common cause of tricuspid regurgitation is
options: acute bacterial endocarditis.
carcinoid tumours.
Ebstein’s anomaly.
mitral or aortic valve disease.
right ventricular failure.

stem: A 47 years old patient underwent a mitral valve repair requiring a quadrangular posterior leaflet resection and ring annuloplasty. After coming off of cardiopulmonary bypass, the transesophageal echocardiogram shows minimal mitral incompetence and moderately severe, unchanged tricuspid regurgitation. The best plan is to
options: close and observe the central venous pressure.
institute pharmacologic afterload reduction.
return to bypass and insert a mechanical tricuspid prosthesis.
return to bypass and repair the tricuspid valve.
return to bypass and replace the mitral valve.

stem: Which of the following structures is located posterior to the mitral valve annulus between the anterior lateral commissure and the mid portion of the posterior leaflet?
options: aortic valve
bundle of His
circumflex coronary artery
membranous septum
coronary sinus

stem: Most of the drainage of the thoracic body wall reaches the superior vena cava via the azygos vein. A notable exception is the left superior intercostal vein, which normally drains into the
options: Left brachiocephalic vein
Left bronchial vein
Left pulmonary vein
Left subclavian vein
Superior vena cava

stem: A malignant growth from the body of the 9th thoracic vertebra exerts pressure anterolaterally. Which structure lies in direct contact with this growth?
options: Right vagus nerve
Right phrenic nerve
Right sympathetic trunk
Right greater thoracic splanchnic nerve
Right 9th intercostal nerve

stem: A frail, elderly man, suspected of having widespread cancer of the lungs and bronchi, is brought in for bronchoscopic examination. The instrument is inserted into the airway, where it accidentally punctures the thin, brittle posterior wall of the diseased right main bronchus. A sudden gush of blood immediately indicates that the instrument has also torn the wall of the blood vessel immediately behind the right main bronchus, i.e., the
options: Azygos vein
Left brachiocephalic artery
Pericardiacophrenic artery
Right pulmonary vein
Superior vena cava

stem: Most chest wall neoplasms are malignant and include lesions that secondarily involve the chest wall via direct invasion or metastasis from intrathoracic tumours or arise as primary tumours. Which of the following statements regarding diagnosis of a chest wall tumour is correct?
options: Pain is usually point-specific.
CT scan is the imaging modality of choice.
MRI cannot accurately evaluate pulmonary nodules.
Incisional biopsy is appropriate for a primary chest wall tumour.
Chondrosarcoma is best diagnosed with needle biopsy.

stem: Tumours of the chest wall are uncommon lesions that represent approximately 5% of all thoracic malignancies. These tumours comprise a heterogeneous group of neoplasms that may arise from osseous structures or soft tissues and may be malignant or benign. Malignant tumours are best treated by chest wall resection. Which of the following statements regarding chest wall resection is correct?
options: A 2 cm margin is adequate for malignant neoplasms.
Rib neoplasms require removal of the entire rib.
Attached structures such as pericardium should be carefully dissected free to protect underlying organs.
Resection of a necrotic tumour is important to extend survival.
Sternal tumours should be “cored” out to preserve the bony thorax.

stem: A positive QRS complex in leads aVR and aVF indicates
options: a normal axis
right axis deviation (RAD)
left axis deviation (LAD)
indeterminate axis
a mean electrical axis between 0° and 90°

stem: In the Randomized On/Off Bypass (ROOBY) Trial, the efficacy of on-pump versus off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting was evaluated. A subanalysis compared the effects on post-bypass patient clinical outcomes and graft patency of endoscopic vein harvesting and open vein harvesting. Which of the following statements regarding the effects on post-bypass patient clinical outcomes and graft patency of endoscopic vein harvesting and open vein harvesting in the ROOBY trial is correct?
options: Endoscopic vein harvest was used in 38% of the cases.
There were no significant differences in both short-term and 1-year composite outcomes between the endoscopic and open groups.
At 1 year follow-up, the saphenous vein graft patency rate for the endoscopic group was similar to that in the open harvest group.
At 1 year follow-up the repeat revascularization rate was significantly lower in the endoscopic group.
Multivariable regression documented significant interaction effect between endoscopic approach and off-pump treatment.

stem: The Placement of Aortic Transcatheter Valves (PARTNER) trial was a multicenter, randomized clinical trial comparing TAVI with standard therapy in high-risk patients with severe aortic stenosis, including a prespecified cohort of patients who were not considered to be suitable candidates for surgery. Which of the following statements regarding the PARTNER trial is correct?
options: Severe aortic stenosis was defined as an aortic-valve area of less than 0.6 cm2.
A left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 40% was an exclusion criterion.
At 1 year the rate of the composite end point of death from any cause or repeat hospitalization was similar with TAVI and standard therapy.
Among survivors at 1 year, the rate of cardiac symptoms was lower among patients who had undergone TAVI than among those who had received standard therapy.
At 30 days, TAVI and standard therapy had a similar incidence of major strokes.

stem: To evaluate the effect of post-operative radiotherapy (PORT) on survival and recurrence in patients with completely resected non-small cell lung cancer the PORT meta-analysis trialists group undertook a systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis to evaluate the available evidence from randomised trials. Which of the following statements regarding the PORT meta-analysis is correct?
options: There was a significant adverse effect of PORT on survival with a hazard ratio of 1.18 or 18% relative increase in the risk of death.
The detrimental effect was most pronounced for patients with stage IIII.
The detrimental effect was most pronounced for patients with N2 disease.
There was no clear evidence of an adverse effect for patients with stage IV.
There was no clear evidence of an adverse effect for patients with N0/NI disease.

stem: In the midregion of the thorax the thoracic duct lies immediately posterior to the
options: aorta
azygos vein
oesophagus
superior vena cava
trachea

stem: An enlarging lymph node gradually constricts the flow of blood in the azygos venous arch. Which vessel would enlarge as a result of collateral drainage?
options: Superior vena cava
Inferior vena cava
Internal thoracic vein
Right brachiocephalic vein
Superior epigastric vein

stem: A 56 years old male with 40 pack year smoking history underwent computerized tomography (CT) scan of the chest to evaluate new onset haemoptysis. The CT scan showed a 5.2 cm spiculated nodule in the right lower lobe with enlarged (>1 cm) ipsilateral mediastinal lymph nodes. What is the stage of this tumour?
options: IA
IIA
IIB
IIIA
IIIB

stem: The role of the coronary sinus is to collect venous blood from the myocardium and deliver this deoxygenated blood to the right atrium. Which of the following statements regarding the coronary sinus and its venous connections is correct?
options: The coronary sinus ostium is located in the anteroseptal area of the right atrium.
The coronary sinus runs transversely in the left atrioventricular groove on the posterior side of the heart close to the distal part of circumflex branch of the left coronary artery.
The middle cardiac vein begins close to the apex of the heart and goes into the posterior interventricular groove.
The anterior cardiac vein enters the coronary sinus close to the coronary sinus ostium.
The middle cardiac vein runs parallel to the left anterior descending artery.

stem: Observational data suggest that the use of bilateral internal mammary arteries (BIMA) during coronary artery bypass graft surgery provides superior revascularization to a single internal mammary artery (SIMA), but concerns about safety have prevented the widespread use of BIMA. The Arterial Revascularisation Trial (ART) is a randomized trial of BIMA vs. SIMA, with a primary outcome of survival at 10 years. Which of the following statements regarding the ART is correct?
options: More deaths were recorded in the BIMA group at 30 days.
The mean number of grafts was significantly more in the BIMA group.
The rates of stroke, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization were lower in the BIMA group at 1 year.
Forty percent of the procedures in both groups were performed off-pump.
Sternal wound reconstruction was similar in both groups at 1 year.

stem: The radial artery (RA), as an alternative to the saphenous vein or the right internal thoracic artery (RITA) for coronary artery bypass grafting, has gained considerable interest over the years. The Radial Artery Patency and Clinical Outcomes (RAPCO) trial is a randomized controlled trial that was undertaken to assess the suitability of the radial artery as a conduit. Which of the following statements regarding RAPCO trial is correct?
options: It is a double-armed randomized controlled trial.
At mid-term the graft patency of the free right internal thoracic artery compared to radial artery was significantly lower in the younger patients.
At mid-term the graft patency of radial artery was significantly superior compared to saphenous vein in the older patients.
The clinical outcomes were inferior for the patients receiving saphenous vein grafts compared to the radial artery grafts in the older patients.
The clinical outcomes were superior for patients receiving free right internal thoracic artery grafts compared to the radial artery grafts in the younger patients.

stem: Aspergilloma is the most common and best recognized form of pulmonary involvement due to Aspergillus. Which of the following statements regarding pulmonary aspergilloma is correct?
options: Most patients with aspergilloma experience symptoms.
The mortality rate from haemoptysis related to aspergilloma ranges between 20% and 40%.
Sputum cultures for Aspergillus spp are positive only in 50% of cases.
Serum IgG antibodies to Aspergillus are positive only in 50% of cases.
Aspergillus antigen recovered from the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of patients with aspergilloma is strongly diagnostic of pulmonary aspergilloma.

stem: Over the past two decades, there has been an increase in the number of anti-reflux operations being performed. This is mostly due to the increasing prevalence of gastroesophageal reflux disease in the population, and the increasing unwillingness of patients to take acid suppressive medications for life. Which of the following statements regarding the anti-reflux operations is correct?
options: The Toupet fundoplication is an anteriorly-placed 270-degree warp.
A total fundoplication is acceptable for all patients.
Prolonged dysphagia after fundoplication is due to poor peristalsis.
A common cause of failure is insufficient reconstruction of the hiatus.
Partial fundoplication has better reflux control with less dysphagia.

stem: Aortic transection injury is a frequently fatal injury secondary to sudden deceleration. Which of the following statements regarding diagnosis and natural history of aortic transection is correct?
options: Transesophageal echocardiography is highly specific but has only fair sensitivity.
Aortography has a 5-10% false-negative rate.
Transesophageal echocardiography is superior to CT for imaging the distal ascending aorta.
The hazard function becomes flat if the patient survives 7 days without treatment.
Up to 20% of patients will die of false aneurysm rupture within 5 years.

stem: Congenital cystic adenomatoid malformations (CCAM) also known as congenital pulmonary airway malformation is a developmental, non-hereditary, hamartomatous abnormality of lung with unknown aetiology. Which of the following statements regarding congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation is correct?
options: Typically one entire lung is involved.
It can be confused with congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
The most common associated anomaly is pectus carinatum.
Prognosis is worst for type I CCAM.
Surgical resection is indicated at the time of diagnosis.

stem: More than one-fourth of adult congenital heart defects are atrial septal defects (ASDs), 75% of which are ostium secundum ASDs. The progressive impact of volume overload of the right cardiac chambers can be halted by ASD closure. Which of the following statements regarding outcomes after surgery for ASD is correct?
options: Survival is equivalent to the general population after repair.
The most common mode of late death is from progressive supraventricular arrhythmias.
Symptomatic improvement occurs in nearly all patients, including those with irreversible cardiomegaly.
Correction of atrial septal defect does not improve AV node conduction.
Recurrence of ASD is most common in young patients with congestive heart failure.

stem: A 45 years old lady is diagnosed with a thymoma. The excised specimen shows macroscopic invasion into surrounding fatty tissue and appears grossly adherent to but not through mediastinal pleura or pericardium. What is the Masaoka stage of this tumour?
options: I
IIA
IIB
III
IVA

stem: Antifibrinolytic agents are commonly used during cardiac surgery to minimize bleeding and to reduce exposure to blood products. The Blood Conservation Using Antifibrinolytics in a Randomized Trial (BART) study was a multicenter, blinded, randomized, controlled study comparing three antifibrinolytic agents commonly used in cardiac surgery. Which of the following statements regarding BART trial is correct?
options: The trial enrolled patients undergoing isolated primary coronary artery bypass grafting.
The trial was terminated early because of the significant superiority of aprotinin compared with tranexamic acid and aminocaproic acid.
The primary outcome was death from any cause at 30 days.
There was a modest reduction in the risk of massive bleeding in the tranexamic acid group compared with aprotinin and aminocaproic acid groups.
There was a strong and consistent negative mortality trend associated with aprotinin.

stem: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is one of the most important primary causes of death after the first year of heart transplantation as well as the most important limiting factor in long-term survival. Which of the following statements regarding cardiac allograft vasculopathy is correct?
options: It has an incidence of 30% at 3 years.
Coronary artery bypass grafting is the best therapeutic option to treat CAV.
The pathogenesis of CAV is attributed to prolonged immunosuppression.
Intravascular ultrasound is the most sensitive tool for diagnosis of CAV.
Coronary cineangiography is the most effective diagnostic investigation for early diagnosis of CAV.

stem: Triple regimen, corticosteroid, calcineurin inhibitor and an antiproliferative agent, continues to be routinely used as the standard immunosuppression for heart transplantation. Calcineurin inhibitors
options: include azathioprine and mycophenolate.
suppress cellular immunity mainly T cells.
stimulate the lipocortin-1 escaping to the extracellular space.
have high immunogenicity.
cause fever, rigors and even anaphylaxis.

stem: A 36 years old female patient is on VA ECMO for failure to wean from cardiopulmonary bypass following a prolonged procedure to treat complex aortic valve and root endocarditis. The nurse managing the patient notices sudden shaking of the venous access line. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is correct?
options: The venous cannula is too big.
The patient is volume overloaded.
The pump head and oxygenator have significant clots.
It is a warning sign for pump head disengagement.
The condition may improve with turning down pump RPM.

stem: Clinical trials have reported lower mortality and repeated revascularization rate in patients treated with coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) as compared to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, these studies were conducted in the era of bare-metal stents. Which of the following statements regarding current best evidence comparing CABG and PCI with drug-eluting stents (DES) in patients with multivessel and/or left main disease is correct?
options: CABG and DES have similar mortality at 5 years.
CABG is associated with significant reduction in myocardial infarction at 1 year.
CABG and DES have similar reduction in repeat revascularization at 1 year.
CABG and DES have similar mortality at 1 year.
CABG and DES have similar stroke rate at 1 year.

stem: The term broncholithiasis is used to denote the presence of calcified or ossified material within the lumen of the bronchus. Broncholithiasis
options: is most commonly caused aspiration of bone tissue or in situ calcification of aspirated foreign material.
most commonly presents with pain, chills, and fever.
being an endobronchial disease is always diagnosed on bronchoscopy.
is best treated bronchoscopically.
usually mimics a tumour.

stem: A pulmonary sequestration is generally defined as nonfunctioning lung tissue that is not in normal continuity with the tracheobronchial tree and that derives its blood supply from systemic vessels. Which of the following statements regarding pulmonary sequestration is correct?
options: In 15%-20% of cases the blood supply of a pulmonary sequestration is from multiple sources.
Intralobar sequestrations account for 25% of all pulmonary sequestrations.
An intralobar sequestration is invested in its own pleural envelope.
The venous drainage of intralobar is usually systemic through the azygos and hemiazygos system or superior vena cava into the right atrium.
Intralobar sequestrations almost always occur within the upper lobes.

stem: Many clinical trials have confirmed that postoperative adjuvant therapy can prolong survival of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the efficiency of postoperative chemotherapy without radiotherapy is unclear, especially in early stage (stages I and II). Which of the following statements regarding current best available evidence for the impact of postoperative chemotherapy without radiotherapy in early stage non-small cell lung cancer patients is correct?
options: Compared with surgery alone, postoperative chemotherapy significantly improves disease-free survival (DFS).
Compared with surgery alone, postoperative chemotherapy has no impact on overall survival (OS).
Single tegafur-uracil (UFT) chemotherapy improves DFS.
Indirect treatment comparison showed cisplatin-based chemotherapy was inferior to single UFT in improving DFS.
Indirect treatment comparison showed cisplatin-based chemotherapy was superior to single UFT in improving OS.

stem: In 2003, the National Emphysema Treatment Trial (NETT) reported the effects of lung volume reduction surgery (LVRS) versus medical treatment on survival and maximum exercise capacity in 1,218 patients who were randomized to treatment between January 1998 and July 2002 and monitored for a mean of 2.4 years. Which of the following statements regarding NETT is correct?
options: The 90-day mortality rate was similar.
Exercise capacity improved by more than 10 W in 28% of patients following after LVRS after 24 months.
The 90-day mortality was similar between median sternotomy and VATS.
Fewer patients required transfusion after VATS compared to median sternotomy.
Median hospital length of stay after LVRS was similar for median sternotomy and VATS patients.

stem: A 56 years old smoker with chronic cough is found to have a 3.2 cm spiculated mass in the left lower lobe in addition to a 1.2 cm spiculated mass in the same lobe. What is the T stage of this tumour?
options: T1a
T1b
T2a
T3
T4

stem: A 45 years old patient with multiple trauma is on the ventilator in the intensive care unit (ICU). If alveolar ventilation is halved (and if CO2 production remains unchanged), then
options: alveolar CO2 pressure (PACO2) will be halved
arterial O2 pressure (PaO2) will double
arterial CO2 pressure (PaCO2) will double
arterial O2 pressure (PaO2) will not change
alveolar O2 pressure (PAO2) will double

stem: You see a patient with damage to the left cervical sympathetic chain ganglia as a result of a neck tumour. Which of the following physical signs would be expected?
options: ptosis (hanging of the upper eye lid) on the left
pupil dilation of the left eye
pale skin on the left side of the face
increased sweat secretion on the left side of the face
lateral deviation of the left eye

stem: Gastrooesophageal reflux disease (GORD) is chronic, very common, and frequently encountered in internal medicine and subspecialty clinics. Which of the following statements regarding gastrooesophageal reflux disease (GORD) is correct?
options: Proton-pump inhibitors heal oesophagitis in about 50% of patients.
A patient with minimal symptomatic relief from medical management is the ideal candidate for surgical intervention.
Columnar-lined esophagus is an indication for surgery.
Atypical symptoms are less likely to respond to surgery.
Antireflux surgery eliminates potential malignant degeneration.

stem: Sarcoidosis is an inflammatory disorder, which can affect any organ system. The lungs are most commonly affected but extrapulmonary sites may cause the initial and/or sole symptoms. Which of the following statements regarding sarcoidosis is correct?
options: It is common in Asian populations.
The aetiology is unknown.
Typical symptoms include a productive cough and dyspnoea.
Peripheral lung biopsy is the usual method for definitive diagnosis
Histology shows caseating granulomas

stem: Primary tumours of the chest wall are uncommon but should be considered in the evaluation of patients with persistent chest wall pain or the presence of a chest wall mass. These tumours comprise a heterogeneous group of neoplasms that may arise from osseous structures or soft tissues and may be malignant or benign. Which of the-following statements regarding malignant chest wall tumours is correct?
options: Chondrosarcomas usually arise in the posterior chest wall.
Rhabdomyosarcomas are extremely painful due to rapid growth.
Chondrosarcoma is associated with prior chest wall radiation.
Adjuvant chemotherapy is the main determinant of survival after resection of a chondrosarcoma.
Most rhabdomyosarcomas occur before age 50.

stem: Double-lumen endotracheal tube placement is performed to achieve lung separation. Left-sided placement of double lumen endobronchial tubes is preferred for most pulmonary resections because:
options: the risk of tearing the membranous wall of the trachea is less.
positioning the tube on the left is easier.
left tubes are larger in internal diameter.
left-sided sleeve resections are facilitated.
left tubes are better at preventing contamination of the operated lung.

stem: An otherwise healthy 38-year-old man complained of shortness of breath. Bronchoscopy showed a red, fleshy mass involving the right upper lobe orifice. A pediatric bronchoscope was able to be advanced past the mass and the bronchus intermedius appeared pristine, as did the middle and lower lobes. The mass was biopsied, resulting in bleeding that was controlled with iced saline lavage. The biopsy was nondiagnostic. The correct action is:
options: repeat bronchoscopy with laser ablation of the mass.
right pneumonectomy.
right upper and middle bilobectomy.
right upper lobe sleeve resection.
right upper lobectomy.

stem: A 24-year-old woman complains of acute right arm swelling and pain. A venogram confirms subclavian vein thrombosis which is successfully treated with catheter-directed thrombolytic therapy. A repeat venogram demonstrates narrowing of the distal subclavian vein and occlusion is elicited by changing the patient's arm position. Which of the following is the best management?
options: immediate heparin therapy followed by coumadin for three months
intravenous stent placement with six weeks of coumadin
resection of the first rib with venolysis
resection of the first rib with vein resection and reconstruction
thrombectomy and patch venoplasty

stem: An osteochondroma is an outgrowth of the growth plate and is made up of both bone and cartilage. Which of the following is the best treatment for a 20-year-old man with an osteochondroma (exostosis) of the lateral right 6th rib?
options: combined radiation and chemotherapy
excision with 4 cm margin, chest wall reconstruction
radiofrequency ablation if symptomatic
radiation and chemotherapy followed by resection
wide local excision

stem: Surgical interruption of intrathoracic autonomic neural pathways has several useful clinical applications, particularly thoracic sympathectomy for upper limb hyperhidrosis and splanchnicectomy for relief of pancreatic pain. The most common complication after thoracoscopic sympathectomy for hyperhidrosis is:
options: compensatory lower extremity sweating.
excessive plantar dryness.
gustatory sweating (Frey's syndrome).
Horner's syndrome.
recurrent hyperhidrosis.

stem: Cystic anomalies of the tracheobronchial tree in infants and children are usually of congenital origin and can be diagnosed with computed tomography and selective use of ultrasonography and arteriography. Which of the following cystic malformations of the tracheobronchial tree is most likely to be asymptomatic when discovered?
options: congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation
congenital lobar emphysema
oesophageal duplication
extralobar pulmonary sequestration
pneumatocoele

stem: A 45-year-old man who was HIV-negative presented with persistent cough. Radiographic studies demonstrated a 3 cm diameter thin-walled cavity in the right upper lobe and adjacent bronchiectasis. Three consecutive sputum cultures identified Mycobacterium avium complex. After an oral regimen of clarithromycin, ethambutol, and rifabutin for six months, his cough resolved. Two monthly sputum cultures continue to demonstrate individual colonies of M. avium. A chest radiograph shows no change in the size of the cavity. The patient is referred for consideration of further therapy. The most appropriate next step is to:
options: change the drug regimen to azithromycin, isoniazid (INH), and streptomycin.
continue current drug treatment.
obtain pulmonary function studies and perfusion scintigraphy.
perform right upper lobectomy with an intrathoracic muscle flap.
perform thoracotomy with wedge resection of the cavity.

stem: Aortic regurgitation is due to incompetence of the aortic valve or any disturbance of the valvular apparatus (eg, leaflets, annulus of the aorta) resulting in the diastolic flow of blood into the left ventricular chamber. Which of the following statements regarding aortic regurgitation is correct?
options: The major pathologic process in rheumatic aortic regurgitation is commissural fusion and thickening of the leaflets.
Annuloaortic ectasia results in aortic regurgitation from annular dilation.
Average survival after the onset of congestive heart failure is less than 2 years.
Syphilitic aneurysms do not cause aortic regurgitation.
One fourth of patients with significant aortic regurgitation survive 5 years after diagnosis.

stem: A 76-year-old active man had an episode of pre-syncope while working in his yard. There was no evidence of seizure activity and he recovered spontaneously. On evaluation he was found to be in sinus rhythm at a rate of 65 beats per minute with stable haemodynamics. He had a cardiac catheterization two years previously that was unremarkable. The most efficient initial workup of this problem is:
options: inpatient echocardiogram and electrophysiologic study (EPS).
inpatient echocardiogram and repeat catheterisation.
inpatient Holter monitoring and EPS.
outpatient catheterisation and EPS.
outpatient echocardiogram and Holter monitoring.

stem: Three months following aortic valve replacement utilising a bioprosthetic valve, a 68-year-old diabetic patient presents with fevers and malaise. Multiple blood cultures are positive for Candida albicans and an echocardiogram shows an 8 mm vegetation on the prosthesis. Proper management is:
options: amphotericin B and thrombolytic therapy.
a full course of amphotericin B followed by aortic valve replacement.
a full course of amphotericin B, serial echocardiography and aortic valve replacement if vegetation size increases.
initial amphotericin B followed by serial blood cultures.
aortic valve replacement after starting amphotericin B therapy.

stem: A 68-year-old man presents with new onset atrial fibrillation and pulmonary oedema. His dyspnoea resolves with medical treatment. He is found to have an ejection fraction of 20% and end-systolic left ventricle diameter of 45 mm. He has a cardiac index of 1.7 L/min/m2, aortic stenosis with a mean systolic gradient of 30 mmHg (valve area 0.9 cm2), and 98% stenosis in the circumflex coronary artery. An MRI scan shows early as well as delayed gadolinium enhancement of the lateral wall. The circumflex system is poorly visualized but it was a large vessel on an angiogram five years ago. The best surgical recommendation is:
options: Do not operate. Even if the patient survives operation, the chance of significant long survival or symptomatic benefit is small.
Perform angioplasty of the circumflex coronary artery. The risk of operation is high and the benefit is limited. Angioplasty has limited benefit also, but the risk is low.
Perform balloon valvuloplasty of the aortic valve. This man is a good candidate for procedure.
Replace the aortic valve with a bioprosthesis. The bioprosthetic valve will last long enough for this patient.
Replace the aortic valve with a mechanical prosthesis. The last thing you want is to have to reoperate for a failed bioprosthesis.

stem: A 56-year-old man with a history of colon cancer resected three years ago had a chest CT scan that demonstrated a new one cm right upper lobe nodule. Metastatic workup was negative. Video assisted wedge resection of the nodule demonstrated a squamous cell carcinoma. The appropriate action is:
options: conclude the procedure and administer adjuvant 5-FU based chemotherapy
conclude the procedure with no adjuvant treatment
perform a completion lobectomy
perform a larger wedge resection to achieve a minimum of 3 cm margins
perform a mediastinal lymph node sampling

stem: A 55-year-old man underwent bronchoscopy for evaluation of a bronchogenic carcinoma of the left hilum. There is a mass at the lobar carina. CT demonstrates no mediastinal adenopathy. Just after the bronchoscopy, the patient coughs up 700 ml of dark blood. The pulmonary angiogram demonstrates a circumferential narrowing of the pulmonary artery in proximity to the left upper lobe bronchus. In the setting of massive haemoptysis these findings are diagnostic of a fistula between pulmonary artery and bronchus. The best management is:
options: bronchial stent
emergent pneumonectomy
endobronchial brachytherapy
left lower lobectomy with bronchial sleeve resection
radiotherapy

stem: A 48-year-old patient has sputum cytology that is positive for cancer, and a normal chest radiograph and chest CT. The correct next step is:
options: fiberoptic bronchoscopy
head and neck examination
MRI of the chest
repeat chest radiograph in 3 months
repeat sputum cytology in 2 months

stem: Valve-sparing aortic root techniques have progressively gained ground in the treatment of aortic root aneurysm and aortic insufficiency. By avoiding anticoagulation therapy they offer a good alternative to composite graft replacement. Which of the following statements regarding valve-sparing aortic root techniques is correct?
options: The root remodeling technique is the most common valve-sparing technique used.
The reimplantation technique is superior to remodeling technique in terms of survival.
Preoperative severe aortic valve regurgitation is associated with a trend towards higher reoperation rate.
Major adverse valve-related events are high following valve-sparing aortic root techniques.
Remodeling technique compared to reimplantation technique is associated with superior valve durability results.

stem: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a feasible interventional technique for severe aortic stenosis in patients who are deemed inoperable or at high surgical risk. There is limited evidence for the safety and efficacy of TAVI in patients with bicuspid aortic valves (BAV), the most common congenital valve abnormality. Which of the following statements regarding outcomes of TAVI in patients with BAV compared to non-BAV is correct?
options: There is a significant increase in 30-day mortality.
There is a significant increase in post-TAVI mean peak gradients.
There is no difference in moderate or severe paravalvular leak.
There is a significant decrease in pacemaker implantations.
There is less conversion to conventional surgery.

stem: Beating-heart on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (BH-ONCAB) offers a hybrid coronary revascularization technique that may confer the benefits of an "off-pump" operation while maintaining the haemodynamic stability and mechanical support of conventional on-pump CABG (C-ONCAB). Which of the following statements regarding outcomes of BH-ONCAB compared to C-ONCAB is correct?
options: There is an increase in 30-day mortality after BH-ONCAB.
There is no difference in midterm survival between BH-ONCAB and C-ONCAB.
C-ONCAB is associated with significantly fewer postoperative myocardial infarction events
Fewer anastomoses are performed with BH-ONCAB.
Fewer strokes occur with BH-ONCAB.

stem: Stentless aortic valves have been reported to provide more physiologic haemodynamic behaviour and cause more timely and thorough regression of ventricular hypertrophy. Which of the following statements regarding stentless compared to stented aortic valves is correct?
options: Mortality for stentless versus stented valve does not differ at 30 days.
Fewer stroke or neurologic complications occur after stentless valve implantation.
Risk of prosthesis-patient mismatch is significantly lower in the stentless group.
Mean gradient is comparable at 3 year follow-up.
Stentless valves are associated with significant improvement in clinical outcomes.

stem: Autologous blood transfusion is a safe and effective method in carefully selected patients undergoing cardiac surgery. Which of the following conditions precludes a patient from being an autologous blood donor?
options: aortic regurgitation
aortic stenosis
left ventricular aneurysm with congestive heart failure
mitral regurgitation
mitral stenosis

stem: A 77-year-old woman underwent four-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting. Four hours after returning to the intensive care unit, her total chest tube drainage is 1300 cc (300-400 cc/hr). She remains haemodynamically stable, and has the following clinical and laboratory values: weight = 55 kg haematocrit = 23% platelet count = 75,000/mm3 International Normalized Ratio (INR) = 1.5 partial thromboplastin time = 32 sec (control = 28 sec) Which of the following interventions is most appropriate?
options: increase the level of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)
open the lower portion of the sternotomy incision at the bedside to assess the level of mediastinal bleeding
return to the operating room for exploration of sternotomy incision
start aprotinin therapy
transfuse fresh-frozen plasma to normalize clotting parameters

stem: A 46-year-old woman is recovering from emergency coronary artery bypass surgery following complications related to a coronary atherectomy procedure. Shortly after extubation she is administered a blood transfusion for a haematocrit of 22%. She subsequently experiences chest tightness, fever, chills, and dyspnoea. Her blood pressure falls and her urine is subsequently noted to be dark red in colour. Which of the following is the most common cause of the transfusion reaction?
options: administration of blood without a filter
bacterial contamination of donor blood
clerical error
mismatches involving the Rh system
overheating of blood during storage

stem: Transvenous pacemaker implantation can be associated with several complications, including myocardial perforation with or without pericardial effusion, venous thrombosis, vegetations of the tricuspid valve or pacing lead, and tricuspid regurgitation. The most common indication for placement of a permanent transvenous pacemaker is
options: chronic bifascicular and trifascicular block.
complete atrioventricular block after cardiac surgery procedure.
intermittent complete heart block.
prolonged atrioventricular block after myocardial infarction.
sick sinus syndrome.

stem: A two month old patient with atresia of the tricuspid valve, ventricular septal defect, normally related great vessels, and no pulmonary stenosis will benefit most from which of the following surgical interventions?
options: patch closure of an atrial septal defect
patch closure of a ventricular septal defect
patch closure of both the atrial and ventricular septal defects
pulmonary artery banding
systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunt

stem: A five year old child is noted to have a murmur of aortic stenosis. Cardiac catheterization demonstrates a peak-to-peak left ventricular-to-aortic gradient of 50 mmHg, mild aortic regurgitation, and the echocardiogram illustrates a trileaflet aortic valve with discrete subvalvular aortic stenosis. Proper management is
options: aortoventriculoplasty (Konno procedure).
continued close follow-up until the gradient increases further or symptoms appear.
open aortic valvotomy.
percutaneous balloon dilatation.
transaortic resection.

stem: The aortogram obtained during cardiac catheterization of a symptomatic child with Williams syndrome shows localized supravalvular aortic stenosis. Of the following procedures, appropriate management is
options: composite aortic root replacement.
Dacron graft replacement of ascending aorta.
open valvotomy on bypass.
patch enlargement of the aorta.
percutaneous balloon dilatation.

stem: A six year old patient underwent closure of a secundum atrial septal defect. At operation a persistent left superior vena cava was noted which was separately cannulated for bypass. The atrial septal defect was closed with a pericardia! patch. Upon weaning from bypass, systemic arterial desaturation is noted. A likely cause is unrecognized
options: anomalous hepatic venous drainage.
anomalous pulmonary venous drainage into the right superior vena cava.
coronary sinus septal defect.
pulmonary valve stenosis.
ventricular septal defect.

stem: The chest radiographs from two different patients below demonstrate popcorn calcification in solitary well defined thoracic lesions. The most likely diagnosis is:
options: bronchogenic cyst
carcinoid
hamartoma
hydatid cyst
pericardial cyst

stem: Axial and sagittal CT images show heterogeneous, well-defined, 6.5 x 24.0 cm, soft tissue mass with speckles of calcification. The most likely diagnosis is
options: adenoid cystic carcinoma
bronchocele
bronchogenic cyst
goiter
hydatid cyst

stem: Coronary artery fistula is a very rare congenital malformation with an abnormal coronary-cameral communication that may involve any chamber and any or all coronary artery branches. Which of the following statements regarding operative technique for repair of coronary arteriovenous fistula?
options: A localised aneurysm over the site of a fistula in the midportion of the right coronary artery should be ligated.
A fistula located in the distribution of the circumflex artery can be safely closed without cardiopulmonary bypass.
Use of a running mattress suture beneath the coronary artery is the most secure method of fistula closure.
Coronary artery bypass grafting may be required for extensive aneurysm formation.
A fistula draining into the pulmonary artery should be ligated externally.

stem: Aortic stenosis is encountered in approximately 5% of children with heart disease. Which of the following statements regarding treatment of congenital valvular aortic stenosis is correct?
options: Division of rudimentary commissures at open valvotomy provides the greatest relief of stenosis.
Aortic root replacement is discouraged in children with a small aortic left ventricular-aortic junction.
Midterm results of percutaneous balloon valvotomy in neonates are equivalent to open valvotomy.
Closed transventricular valvotomy is superior to percutaneous valvotomy.
Excision of fibrous nodules or thickening should be avoided to prevent leaflet perforation.

stem: Infective endocarditis occurs worldwide, and is defined by infection of a native or prosthetic heart valve, the endocardial surface, or an indwelling cardiac device. The causes and epidemiology of the disease have evolved in recent decades with a doubling of the average patient age and an increased prevalence in patients with indwelling cardiac devices. Which of the following statements regarding infective endocarditis is correct?
options: Aortic valve abscess typically occurs below the commissure between the right and left coronary cusps.
Mitral valve ring abscess usually is found at the anterosuperior aspect of the annulus.
Tissue valves are more resistant to infection than mechanical valves.
Minimal debridement of the mitral anulus should be performed to prevent atrioventricular discontinuity.
Local irrigation with amphotericin may be helpful in fungal endocarditis.

stem: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has emerged as a feasible alternative treatment to conventional surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR) for high-risk patients with aortic stenosis. Which of the following statements regarding current best available evidence comparing TAVI and AVR is correct?
options: There is no difference in mortality.
There is a significantly increased stroke rate after conventional AVR.
There is a significantly increased acute renal failure rate after TAVI.
There is a significantly increased myocardial infarction rate after TAVI.
The patients who have conventional AVR require more permanent pacemakers.

stem: Mitral valve repair was performed for mitral regurgitation. The procedure included resection of a flail segment of the middle scallop of the posterior leaflet and ring annuloplasty. Bypass was weaned, but haemodynamics were borderline with elevated filling pressures and a cardiac index of 1.8 L/(min*m2). There was no improvement with inotropic drugs. The transesophageal echocardiogram is shown. Appropriate therapy is:
options: intra-aortic balloon pump support
bypass the circumflex coronary artery
pharmacologic afterload reduction
mitral valve replacement
removal of the annuloplasty ring

stem: A 75-year-old man presents with dull right subcostal pain and chronic constipation. A chest radiograph is shown below. Which of the following statements about this condition is correct?
options: Defects on the left are more common than on the right.
It results from a defect in the space of Larrey.
Recurrence is high (>25%) after primary surgical repair.
Repair is best achieved by a transthoracic approach.
This is more common in thin than obese patients.

stem: The barium swallow below shows sliding (type I) oesophageal hiatal hernia. Which of the following statements regarding sliding (Type I) oesophageal hiatal hernias is correct?
options: They are more common, and larger, in patients with Barrett's oesophagus.
They are infrequently found in the general population.
They are less common than paraoesophageal (Type II) hiatal hernias.
They are usually irreducible in the upright position.
Ulceration, bleeding, or strangulation are common complications.

stem: Barrett's-associated oesophageal adenocarcinoma is the fastest rising cancer in the developed world. Which of the following statements regarding surveillance of Barrett's oesophagus is correct?
options: Barrett's surveillance is cost effective when compared with other cancer surveillance programs.
Fifteen percent of patients with high-grade dysplasia on biopsy have invasive cancer at oesophagectomy.
Gastric and intestinal columnar epithelium are strongly associated with adenocarcinoma development.
Subtle mucosal irregularities in areas of Barrett's mucosa are of little prognostic significance.
The overall mortality rate of patients with Barrett's oesophagus is twice that of the general population.
